jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

OpenObserve is a fast-growing, developer-forward observability platform built for modern, high-scale systems. We help engineering teams ship faster and sleep better by making logs, metrics, and traces simpler, faster, and far more cost-efficient. A cloud-native architecture and smart indexing deliver real-time insight without the usual complexity or runaway costs.

We're backed by Nexus Venture Partners and Dell Technologies Capital. The open-source project has more than 22K GitHub stars and 10K active deployments, and our customers include some of the largest engineering organizations in the world. They choose OpenObserve to unify observability, cut spend, and speed up incident response.

Our culture is product-obsessed, customer-driven, and high ownership. We move quickly, value clarity, and give people room to take big swings.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer, you'll own the customer's technical journey with OpenObserve, and it starts before the contract is signed. You'll work alongside sales during proofs of concept, take pilots through to full deployment, and then make sure customers get what they bought OpenObserve for and stay with us for years.

This is a technical role. Our customers are platform engineers, SREs, and DevOps leaders, many of them mid-migration from Datadog, Splunk, or Elastic. They'll expect you to understand their architecture, get your hands into the product, and have an opinion about what good observability looks like.

It's a good fit if you come from engineering, SRE, or support and have found that the part of the job you like most is working with the people who use what you build. You'll keep your hands in the technology and spend most of your week with customers. We'll coach you on the commercial side.

It is also not a support role, and the difference matters to us. Support is reactive: a ticket comes in, it gets fixed, it gets closed. Success is proactive: you know what the customer is trying to achieve, you notice when they're drifting away from it, and you act before they have to ask. You'll work closely with support and engineering and you'll own escalations, but your job isn't to close tickets. It's the outcome.

OTE: $140K–$170K (80/20 split), plus equity.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Twelve months in, four things are true:

 1. Your customers renew, and most are sending more data than when you started. Retention and growth in your portfolio are the scoreboard.

 2. Pilots become deployments. Customers who started with a POC are in full production and off their incumbent, on the timeline they were promised.

 3. You see problems before the customer does. A drop in usage, a champion who left, a team that never onboarded. You caught it and did something about it.

 4. The function is better than you found it. Onboarding, health scoring, and business reviews are documented and repeatable, so the next person we hire starts ahead.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - POCs and pilots: Join evaluations before the contract is signed. Work with the account executive to agree success criteria, get the customer's data flowing, and make sure the pilot proves what it needs to prove.

 - Pilot to full deployment: Take customers from a successful pilot to production at full scale. Plan the cutover from their existing tools, get data sources, pipelines, dashboards, and alerts in place, and keep the project on schedule.

 - Adoption and outcomes: Build a success plan for each account tied to what the customer cares about, whether that's cost, incident response time, or coverage. Track usage and health, and act on early warning signs.

 - Technical guidance: Review architecture, ingestion, retention, and query performance. Recommend what to change and show them how, in the product, not on a slide.

 - Relationships: Build trust with the engineers who use OpenObserve every day and with the leaders who signed for it. Run business reviews people want to attend.

 - Renewals and expansion: Own or partner with sales on renewals. Spot expansion when a new team, data source, or use case appears, and work with the account executive to close it.

 - Escalations: When something breaks, coordinate support and engineering and keep the customer informed. You own the customer's experience even when you don't own the fix.

 - Voice of the customer: Bring patterns from your accounts to product and engineering, with enough detail that they can act on them.

 - The playbook: Write the POC templates, onboarding guides, migration runbooks, and training content that make the next customer faster than the last.


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO

The best people in this job are part engineer, part consultant, part diplomat. They can debug an ingestion pipeline in the morning and talk a frustrated VP through a renewal in the afternoon, and they're interested in both.

 - Has 4+ years in a technical role such as software engineering, SRE, DevOps, support engineering, or solutions engineering, and wants to spend more of the week with customers. Prior customer success or technical account management experience is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Has real observability experience. You've used, run, or supported tools like Datadog, Splunk, Elastic, Grafana, or New Relic, and you have opinions about what good monitoring looks like.

 - Is technical enough to be credible with engineers. You're comfortable with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, OpenTelemetry, and log, metric, and trace pipelines. You can write SQL, read a config file, and reproduce a problem yourself before you escalate it.

 - Understands the difference between support and success. You don't measure your week in tickets closed. You measure it in whether your customers are getting closer to what they set out to do.

 - Has high emotional intelligence. You hear the frustration under a polite email. You know when an engineer wants an answer and when an executive wants reassurance. You can deliver bad news without getting defensive and without losing the room.

 - Is smart and curious. You want to know why something works, not just that it does. You'll dig into a customer's stack because you find it interesting, and you learn new technology fast.

 - Communicates clearly, in writing and in person, with hands-on engineers and with executives.

 - Has commercial sense, or wants to build it. You don't need to have owned a renewal before, but you're curious about how the business side works and can tell an expansion opportunity from a favor.

 - Is organized. You can run a portfolio of accounts and several evaluations and migrations at once without dropping things.

 - Thrives in early-stage environments. You're comfortable with ambiguity and would rather build the process than inherit it.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Impact: An early seat in customer success, with direct access to the CRO and real influence on how we win, onboard, retain, and grow customers.

 - A path toward customers: If you're coming from an engineering role, you'll get coaching from the CRO on the customer and commercial side while staying close to the technology.

 - Compensation: Competitive base, bonus tied to retention and growth, and meaningful equity.

 - Product: An open-source-rooted product with clear technical differentiation and customers who love it. You'll be representing something you can be proud of.

 - Benefits: Full benefits, flexible schedule, and unlimited PTO.

 - Growth: Paths to senior and strategic customer success, solutions architecture, or leading the team as we scale.


LOCATION

Remote, United States. Timezone overlap for core collaboration hours required; occasional travel for customer visits, events, and team offsites.

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer - Thermophotovoltaic Hardware & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

Position Summary

You will own the design, sourcing, and manufacturing of the structural and thermal hardware interfacing with Antora's thermophotovoltaic (TPV) modules. Our Heat-to-Power team builds TPV heat engines that convert stored high-temperature radiant heat into electricity, and we need an engineer who can turn our working TPV assembly into a product we can build reliably at low cost. Your first project is designing, prototyping, and testing our next-generation TPV assembly: large extruded cold plates with removable TPV modules on direct bonded copper (DBC) substrates. After that, you will carry each new generation of TPV hardware into production by building our supplier base, driving DFM and cost-down, and improving performance and reliability. You will partner with our architecture lead, who owns system concept and analysis, and work closely with thermal, electrical, and test engineers at our R&D facility.

Roles & Responsibilities

• Own the mechanical design of TPV hardware from concept through production release.

• Design, prototype, and test our next-generation TPV assembly, including large extruded aluminum cold plates and a reversible attachment for DBC-based TPV modules.

• Frame thermal simulation requests for our thermal engineers (the question, inputs, boundary conditions, and the decision each result informs), and run first-order thermal models yourself to screen options before committing to hardware.

• Use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) throughout the work, from supplier packages and cost models to analysis scripts and first-order thermal models.

• Produce release-ready detailed drawings with GD&T and tolerance stack-ups, and set the standard for drawing quality on TPV hardware.

• Build and manage our supplier base of machine shops, extruders, and fabricators: run RFQs, evaluate capability and cost, manage lead times, own first-article inspection and supplier quality issues.

• Drive DFM/DFA and cost-down: own the BOM and cost model, and reduce part count, assembly steps, and failure points such as coolant connections.

• Get hardware built through hands-on prototyping, assembly, and fixture design.

• Plan and run thermal, pressure, leak, and reliability tests with our test team to qualify designs.

• Carry each new generation of TPV hardware into production, including sourcing, qualification, and continuous improvement.

• Document designs, assembly procedures, and inspection criteria so hardware can be built and serviced repeatedly.

Key Qualifications

• 5+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience, including hardware you carried from prototype into production.

• Deep, practical knowledge of manufacturing processes such as CNC machining, extrusion, brazing, welding, and sheet metal, and of what drives cost, lead time, and yield.

• Extensive direct work with machine shops, fabricators, and contract manufacturers: RFQs, supplier selection, first-article inspection, and resolving quality issues.

• Expert at release-ready detailed drawings, including GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis.

• Proficient in 3D CAD and PDM/PLM release workflows.

• Hands-on builder: comfortable assembling, fixturing, and testing prototypes yourself.

• Experience designing liquid-cooled or thermally loaded hardware such as cold plates, heat exchangers, seals and fluid fittings, or thermal interface materials.

• Experience working with thermal analysts: framing the question, specifying inputs and boundary conditions, and critically interpreting simulation results before acting on them.

• Clear written and verbal communication, and experience leading design reviews across mechanical, thermal, electrical, and test disciplines.

• Fluent with Claude, ChatGPT, or similar AI tools in day-to-day engineering work, such as drafting RFQs and specifications, comparing supplier quotes, checking tolerance stacks, writing analysis scripts, and setting up first-order thermal models.

• BS, MS or Ph.D in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.

• Ability to work onsite.

Additional Qualifications Desired

• Power electronics or semiconductor module packaging: DBC or AMB substrates, baseplates, direct-cooled modules, EV traction inverters, or similar.

• Vacuum or controlled-atmosphere hardware.

• Reliability and qualification testing: thermal cycling, pressure and leak testing, failure analysis.

• Structural FEA for design checks such as clamping, flatness, and thermal stress.

• Cost-down and production ramp experience at a startup or scaling manufacturer.

• Background in photovoltaics, energy conversion, or other energy hardware.

Work Location:  Onsite - Sunnyvale, CA

Salary Range:  $115,000 USD - $210,000 USD

Salary Basis:  Annual

Please note that the salary range listed above reflects Antora Energy's estimated pay for this position. The actual salary offered will be within the posted range and determined based on several factors including but not limited to a candidate's experiences, credentials and expertise, as they pertain to the position's requirements.

In addition to a competitive base salary, Antora Energy’s Total Rewards program includes equity compensation in the form of stock options, a premium health benefits package with life and disability insurance, a 401K plan with employer contributions, flexible spending accounts, and an industry leading paid-time-off policy that features flexible and inclusive holiday observance, as well as paid volunteer time off.

#LI-Onsite

When it comes to stopping climate change, we need everyone. We believe that having a diversity of backgrounds and experiences strengthens all of us, and we strive to create an environment where every one of us is empowered to create meaningful change.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Advanced Pilot Assistant Software (Autonomy/Robotics)
jobs.description:
ABOUT BEACON AI

We’re a fast-moving team of aviators, engineers, and operators building an AI platform to make flying safer, more efficient, and more capable. Backed by top investors, we’ve secured a dozen Department of Defense contracts and partnered with major airlines to deliver mission-critical systems. We operate without silos or heavy processes. Small, focused teams own what they build, ship quickly, and learn fast, pushing the boundaries of how humans and AI work together in aviation.



Role Overview

We are seeking a Software Engineer to help design and build the advanced pilot assistance software that supports our flight safety platform. In this role, you will develop and deploy autonomy, robotics, and embedded systems that operate in real-world, safety-critical aviation environments. You will contribute hands-on across the stack, working closely with senior engineers to deliver reliable systems that support time-sensitive decision-making for human operators.

What You’ll Do

 - Design, build, and deploy robotic and embedded software components used in advanced pilot assistance systems.

 - Contribute to autonomy-related features or subsystems from development through deployment, with a focus on reliability and performance.

 - Write, test, and maintain high-quality Python and/or C++ code across autonomy, systems, and embedded components.

 - Integrate software with hardware, sensors, and perception or data ingestion pipelines to support autonomous and operator-in-the-loop decision-making.

 - Help optimize software for edge compute environments, including managing latency and resource usage.

 - Participate in testing, validation, and deployment efforts to ensure systems meet safety-critical and mission-critical requirements.

 - Collaborate in design reviews, code reviews, and hands-on development with senior engineers and cross-functional teams.

What Will Make You Successful

 - 2+ years of experience designing or building robotic software and/or embedded systems, or equivalent experience through projects, internships, or coursework.

 - Experience writing production-quality code in C++ and/or Python.

 - Familiarity with real-time or interactive systems that support users making time-sensitive decisions.

 - Exposure to autonomy-related systems such as planning, decision-making, or reasoning, and working with sensor or perception pipelines.

 - Some experience working with embedded or edge compute platforms and debugging hardware/software interactions.

 - Ability to learn quickly and contribute effectively in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

Bonus Points

 - Experience working on safety-critical or mission-critical systems, including aviation or robotics domains.

 - Exposure to robot operating systems or middleware such as ROS or DDS.

 - Interest in human-in-the-loop systems, simulation environments, or real-time control systems.

 - Background or strong interest in autonomy, robotics, or advanced mobility.

Work Location
This is a hybrid role based in San Carlos, CA, with 3+ days per week onsite and the option to work remotely on remaining days.

Perks & Benefits (Full-Time Employees)

 - Healthcare: 100%* of employee medical premiums covered; 25% for dependents

 - Time Off: 3 weeks PTO plus 13+ paid company holidays

jobs.title: Senior Aerothermal Analysis Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Aerothermal Analysis Engineer

Location: Playa Vista, California (in-person, five days per week)

The return lane isn’t going to build itself. Come build it with us.

Outpost is an orbital logistics company rewriting the rules of global logistics by building reusable Earth-return vehicles that unlock in-space manufacturing, on-orbit warehousing, and 60-minute global delivery through space.

Our CarryAll vehicle family returns payloads ranging from 200 kilograms to 10 metric tons, lands within 10 meters of its target, and can then be refurbished and launched again. One vehicle, many missions: responsive logistics and precision delivery for national security; commercial cargo moved with real cadence; R&D payloads flown, tested, and refined across repeatable cycles; and critical aid delivered where roads and runways can’t reach.

The demand is already here, validated through defense and civil agreements and supported by a growing pipeline of government and commercial customers.

We have the customers, the team, and a clear technical path ahead of us. We’re building the return lane. Come build it with us.

The Role

The Senior Aerothermal Analysis Engineer will own the aerothermal environments for CarryAll, combining high-fidelity CFD, engineering-level methods, and test data into the database that drives thermal protection system (TPS) sizing, structural design, and trajectory. On every return, CarryAll's deployable heatshield and structure pass through very different flow regimes as the vehicle slows from Mach 25, from rarefied upper-atmosphere flow through peak heating and down to subsonic descent. Because CarryAll is built to fly again, the environments don't just size a heatshield for one flight; they define how the thermal protection system holds up across many.

Responsibilities

• Own aerothermal environment definition for CarryAll across its full flight envelope, from early trade studies through flight, and keep it current as the design evolves.

• Set up and run high-enthalpy CFD at the key trajectory points that anchor the environments, capturing thermochemical non-equilibrium effects where they matter.

• Bridge the gaps between CFD points with fast engineering heating methods, so every trajectory and attitude of interest has a credible answer without a full solve.

• Combine CFD, engineering estimates, and ground and flight test results into a single environment product with clearly stated uncertainties and margins.

• Work alongside Guidance Navigation and Control (GNC) engineers and hardware owners such as TPS, structures, and mechanism engineers to define environments that set TPS thickness, structural temperatures, and trajectory limits for flight hardware.

• Add solver capability when standard tools can't capture the physics, such as custom US3D subroutines for finite-rate chemistry, ablation products, and CarryAll-specific boundary conditions.

• Prove out new and existing methods against analytical cases, arc-jet and wind tunnel tests, and flight data.

• Automate environment generation and delivery so updates keep pace with design iterations.

• Managing and maintaining compute resources.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or higher in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering.

• 5+ years of experience in hypersonic, supersonic, reentry, or rocketry aerothermodynamic analysis.

• Experience running high-enthalpy flow solvers (FUN3D, US3D, DPLR or similar).

• Experience with parallel scientific computing (e.g., MPI), high-performance computing environments, and large-scale CFD campaign automation.

• Experience with handbook and engineering-level heating estimation methods (e.g., Fay-Riddell, Tauber, MINIVER-class tools, or similar correlations).

• Strong fundamentals in hypersonic aerodynamics, boundary layer physics, and convective and radiative heat transfer.

• Experience modeling high-temperature gas dynamics and chemistry, including thermochemical non-equilibrium.

• Proficiency in programming languages like Python, Fortran, C++, or MATLAB for analysis tooling and automation.

• Proven ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with rapid iteration.

Preferred Experience

• Active U.S. Government Security Clearance (Not required, but beneficial).

• Master's or PhD in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering, or an equivalent field.

• Direct experience with FUN3D, including extension through user-defined subroutines.

• Experience developing aerodynamic databases.

• Experience with uncertainty quantification and the definition of design margins for aerothermal environments.

• Experience integrating ground and flight test data into aerothermal vehicle models.

• Experience with boundary layer transition prediction and its treatment in heating environments.

• Experience with deployable or flexible decelerators and thermal protection systems (e.g., HIAD, ADEPT) or reusable TPS.

• Familiarity with Fidelity Pointwise or equivalent meshing software for generating high-quality meshes.

• Experience modeling radiative heating using radiation transport tools.

• Familiarity with TPS sizing and material response tools (e.g., FIAT, CHAR) as downstream consumers of environments.

• Experience contributing to an aerothermal database effort from a vehicle's early design stages through first flight.

• Involvement in planning, leading, and/or post-processing wind tunnel or arc-jet test campaigns.

• Prior experience working in startups and/or small independent teams.

Compensation:

• Competitive compensation: $170,000 - $225,000 annual salary; (commensurate with experience).

• Additional Compensation: Annual performance-based bonuses that reward your impact.

• Shared upside: Meaningful equity in Outpost so you share directly in the value you help create.

• Comprehensive healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision coverage to keep you and your loved ones covered. We cover the base tier of medical insurance and all premiums of vision and dental.

• Protection when it matters: Company-provided short- and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind, plus life insurance for even more security.

• PTO: Recharge on your own terms with paid time off, plus 9 days of paid holidays.

• Invest in your future:401(k) with company match to help you build long-term wealth.

• Fueled for the mission: Daily DoorDash lunch stipend, plus unlimited snacks, coffee, and tea to keep you energized.

• Mission that matters: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with leaders from aerospace, new space, and deep-tech industries building the future of orbital infrastructure.

• Pet Friendly Office: Bring your furry friend into the office so that they can be a part of our mission too.

• Monthly Company Happy Hours and Events: Drinks at the local bar, hibachi nights, mini golfing and more!

You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15, or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S.

jobs.title: Environmental Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
About the role

Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California.

The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space.

You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft.

Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.

Responsibilities

• Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing.

• Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment.

• Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns.

• Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing.

• Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations.

• Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements.

• Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows.

• Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems.

• Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis.

• Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers.

• Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities.

• Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment.

Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems.

• Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development.

• Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.

• Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing.

• Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing.

• Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment.

• Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports.

• Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation.

• Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis.

• Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.

• Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements.

• Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing.

Pay range

Bachelor's students $40/hour

Master's $45/hour

PhD $50/hour

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.  Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. jobs.title: Senior Avionics Test Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As an Avionics Test Engineer, you'll play a key role in the design and operation of critical systems that simulate and stress-test flight hardware to prove it is ready for its trip to space. Your work will be instrumental in ensuring the success of our Winnebago-class spacecraft and future ambitious projects. Your expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry. This is your opportunity to contribute to technologies that are defining the future of space exploration and make an impact that reaches far beyond the stars.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate test systems for spacecraft avionics components and assemblies to fully exercise components during environmental stress testing and component acceptance testing.

• Develop software in Python to implement and execute test procedures, analyze test data, assess pass/fail criteria, and generate test reports.

• Collaborate with component Responsible Engineers (REs) to identify test cases and develop innovative testing strategies to ensure avionics products meet their intended performance standards across extreme conditions.

• Craft comprehensive test plans for flight hardware, manage and conduct qualification, acceptance, and proto-flight tests.

• Work closely with avionics test systems engineers and manufacturing engineers to standardize test software behavior, user interfaces, and data reporting.

• Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.

• Collaborate with avionics systems and flight software engineers to develop and operate Hardware in the Loop (HITL) testbeds to simulate the spacecraft on the ground and ensure all systems are mission-ready.

• Draw from your experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• At least 5 years of experience in system validation, component testing, or test software development with at least 3 years working on aerospace test systems.

• Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.

• Experience with electronics test equipment including power supplies, DAQ systems, electronic loads, oscilloscopes and multimeters.

• Familiarity with common sensor types, including thermocouples, RTDs and 4-20mA devices.

• Proficiency with Git source control system.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments.

• Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.

• Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).

• Strong project or program management skills.

• Thrive in a dynamic work environment that values teamwork, innovation, and tackling challenges head-on. Be prepared for exposure to diverse tasks and a commitment to personal and professional growth.

Pay Range

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Benefits

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first https://blog.junipersquare.com/juniper-square-ponders-future-of-office-with-digital-first-hybrid-workplace-strategy/ operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time.




ABOUT YOUR ROLE

We are hiring a few Senior Associates to join our team. This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast paced start-up environment to help build out Juniper Square’s Fund Administration service offering. Juniper Square is on a mission to transform the Fund Administration offering to Private Markets. We are more than a Fund Administrator, we are a Modern Fund Administrator.  As a Senior Fund Accountant you will partner with the customer, other members of the fund accounting team, and Investor Services and Fund Administration Onboarding teams to deliver  fund accounting and reporting services to Juniper Square’s Private Market customers in the Real Estate, Private Equity, and Venture Capital space. You will have a significant opportunity to shape the trajectory of our service offering and in so doing help to deliver a best-in-class experience to our customers. We are a team of values based self-starters with a curious mindset and the motivation to use technology to our advantage so that we are continually iterating and improving on the status quo. This is an opportunity to couple prior education and experience and to learn from some of the best talent in Private Markets.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support  major decisions regarding team buildout and operational policies and procedures

 - Define and support the implementation of fund administration workflows, applying best practices and process efficiencies

 - Interface directly with clients to deliver an outstanding client experience

 - Serve as a technical accounting expert and key advisor on significant business/accounting decisions for the team

 - Perform accounting, analytical, & financial reporting duties; ensure client and investor reporting is prepared and completed timely and accurately

 - Review waterfall calculations and capital calls and distributions in accordance with clients’ Limited Partnership Agreements

 - Prepare and review asset- and fund-level performance metrics (IRRs, TVPI, etc.)

jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As an Avionics Test Engineer, you'll play a key role in the design and operation of critical systems that simulate and stress-test flight hardware to prove it is ready for its trip to space. Your work will be instrumental in ensuring the success of our Winnebago-class spacecraft and future ambitious projects. Your expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry. This is your opportunity to contribute to technologies that are defining the future of space exploration and make an impact that reaches far beyond the stars.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate test systems for spacecraft avionics components and assemblies to fully exercise components during environmental stress testing and component acceptance testing.

• Develop software in Python to implement and execute test procedures, analyze test data, assess pass/fail criteria, and generate test reports.

• Collaborate with component Responsible Engineers (REs) to identify test cases and develop innovative testing strategies to ensure avionics products meet their intended performance standards across extreme conditions.

• Craft comprehensive test plans for flight hardware, manage and conduct qualification, acceptance, and proto-flight tests.

• Work closely with avionics test systems engineers and manufacturing engineers to standardize test software behavior, user interfaces, and data reporting.

• Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.

• Collaborate with avionics systems and flight software engineers to develop and operate Hardware in the Loop (HITL) testbeds to simulate the spacecraft on the ground and ensure all systems are mission-ready.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• At least 3 years of experience in system validation, component testing, or test software development.

• Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.

• Experience with electronics test equipment including power supplies, DAQ systems, electronic loads, oscilloscopes and multimeters.

• Familiarity with common sensor types, including thermocouples, RTDs and 4-20mA devices.

• Proficiency with Git source control system.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager

Brain Corp is a San Diego, California, USA-based AI company creating transformative core technology for the robotics industry. Our purpose is to create autonomous technology that helps the real world work better. Brain's robotic and AI solutions help retailers ensure that the right product is on the right shelf at the right price, in a clean environment. Through the BrainOS® Robotics Platform, which powers the largest global fleet of the Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) in operation in commercial public spaces, Brain Corp delivers insightful and efficient automated solutions in both commercial floor cleaning and inventory management, empowering organizations and their employees to achieve more. Brain Corp currently powers more than 30,000 AMRs, representing the largest fleet of its kind in the world. Brain Corp is funded by the SoftBank Vision Fund, Clearbridge, and Qualcomm Ventures.

Named a top workplace by the San Diego Union Tribune and USA today in 2025, we make life-changing impacts through innovation, helping workers globally unlock their abilities in orchestration with intelligent machines.

As a Senior Product Manager, you will identify market problems, use cases, and outcomes for our AI and autonomy platform, BrainOS®, and associated product lines.

Brain Corp is a customer-driven company, meaning you will engage directly with end-users and manufacturers to understand their problems and define opportunities. You will partner closely with engineering, program management, and other stakeholders to increase customer delight, drive sales, and deliver the right business outcomes. • Other duties and projects as assigned

• A gritty problem-solver who thrives on wearing multiple hats, rolling up their sleeves, and executing in the details

The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for the assembly, integration, and validation of spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and testing. As an Industrial Engineering Intern, you will support the development and improvement of the processes, tools, and systems that enable Muon to efficiently build and test spacecraft at scale.

You will work closely with AIT, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Test Engineering teams to analyze production data, improve workflows, identify bottlenecks, develop capacity models, and implement process improvements. This is a hands-on opportunity to apply industrial engineering principles in a fast-growing spacecraft manufacturing environment and directly contribute to increasing production efficiency and throughput.

Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.

Responsibilities

• Analyze spacecraft assembly, integration, and test processes to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, throughput, and scalability.

• Develop and maintain process maps, standard work, work instructions, and other manufacturing documentation.

• Collect and analyze production data to identify trends, bottlenecks, constraints, and opportunities for improvement.

• Support development of production capacity and resource planning models for spacecraft assembly and test operations.

• Assist with production scheduling, workflow optimization, and resource allocation across AIT operations.

• Conduct time studies and process observations to establish baseline cycle times, labor requirements, and process performance.

• Support development and implementation of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Identify opportunities to improve material flow, kitting, tooling, workstation layout, and overall factory/lab utilization.

• Develop dashboards, reports, and other data-driven tools to provide visibility into production performance and operational metrics.

• Support root-cause investigations and corrective actions for production constraints, process inefficiencies, and recurring issues.

• Partner with technicians and engineers to identify practical improvements to spacecraft assembly and test processes.

• Support implementation and validation of process improvements on the production floor.

• Assist with developing scalable processes and systems to support increasing spacecraft production volume.

• Document process improvements and communicate findings and recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders.

Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field.

• Strong understanding of engineering, manufacturing, and/or operations fundamentals.

• Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data to identify process improvements.

• Experience with Excel or similar tools for data analysis, modeling, and visualization.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.

• Ability to work hands-on in a production, laboratory, or engineering environment.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to approach complex operational challenges from a first-principles perspective.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Previous internship, co-op, research, or project experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing, operations, or production environments.

• Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, value-stream mapping, or other continuous improvement methodologies.

• Experience conducting time studies, capacity analysis, line balancing, or process optimization.

• Experience with production planning, scheduling, or resource capacity modeling.

• Experience with data visualization or analytics tools such as Python, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar.

• Experience with CAD or facility/workstation layout tools.

• Experience developing automated spreadsheets, dashboards, or other operational tools.

• Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.

• Familiarity with manufacturing, assembly, integration, or test processes for complex electromechanical hardware.

• Experience working in a cleanroom, laboratory, or aerospace manufacturing environment.

Pay range

Bachelor's students $40/hour

Master's $45/hour

PhD $50/hour

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a motivated individual with a scientific background to play a critical role as the strategic sourcing and supplier management lead for drug product and finished product within the Pharmaceutical Development and Manufacturing (PDM) function. This position will be responsible for business and technical operations in support of PDM outsourcing activities and leading strategic initiatives to enable planning, sourcing, production, and delivery of Revolution Medicines’ drug supply, with focus on drug product and finished product. This role is an individual contributor with cross-functional team leadership responsibilities, reporting into the Director, Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management.

Responsibilities:

• Responsible for ongoing management of RevMed’s global network of Drug Product Manufacturers.

• Drive implementation of RevMed’s CMO Lifecycle Management Program across our network of Drug Product CMOs. Support identification, selection, on-boarding, start-up and ongoing management of CMO’s.

• Lead CMO management activities, including business and manufacturing support, issue resolution, and performance management. Lead weekly cross-functional site leadership team meetings with CMO to ensure all start-up and production activities are conducted successfully on-time.

• Understand CMO partner internal structure and processes and work with team to ensure successful production, issue resolution and communication takes place to meet RevMed’s production requirements.

• Lead site issue management and resolution during routine production and escalate issues, when appropriate. Drive risk management activities, including the identification of risks and creation of mitigation plans. Support product transfer activities to the CMO.

• Establish and maintain effective relationships with key CMO stakeholders to ensure successful manufacture and issue resolution across the external manufacturing network. Foster collaborative relationships with internal stakeholders (e.g. Clinical Operations, Development, Regulatory, Quality, Operations, Finance, etc.) to understand organizational needs.

• Create and manage contracts, requests for pricing, supply agreements, etc. Ensure activities are executed in alignment with established Supply and Quality Agreements. Work with stakeholders and suppliers to help drive business issues to resolution. Understand contractual / financial implications of issues and solutions and ensure appropriate outcomes are implemented. Manage and communicate forecasts to the sites. Support capacity planning activities.

• Manage CMO Performance. Measure and report on the overall performance of each CMO. Identify and drive performance improvements (COGS, cycle time, quality, etc.) to ensure efficient, reliable supply of all clinical and commercial products.

• Work collaboratively with Project Management to ensure projects from conception to implementation and close-out, as directed by management.

• Serve as Revolution Medicines’ primary business operation lead and project management interface between internal PDM functions and CRDMOs for drug product and finished product by providing adequate oversight.

• Ensure projects/programs meet desired results, compliance, speed, quality, and cost.

• Support cross-functional CRDMO management activities, covering all aspects such as business needs identification, market screening, contracting, vendor qualification and set-up, compliant delivery of services, and discontinuation.

• Work with PDM senior management and cross-functional teams to assess and manage supplier performance through use of personal influence, internal business review meetings, and/or joint governance meetings.

• Identify and deliver on cost savings opportunities.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• B.Sc. or M.Sc. in scientific field with 15+ years of experience in pharmaceutical strategic sourcing and/or supply chain.

• Experience working with domestic and international CRDMOs.

• Experience managing both strategic and tactical/operational projects.

• Working knowledge of and experience in clinical manufacturing, regulatory, QA, and cGMP requirements for small molecules.

• Working knowledge of small molecule drug development and commercialization, including, but not limited to, oral solid dosage form development and manufacturing, scale-up, and validation.

• Working knowledge of pharma end-to-end supply chain, with oral solid dosage form related supply a plus.

• Strong negotiation skills.

• Solid project management, facilitation, and problem solving skills.

• Solid organizational and time management skills.

• Effective, open, and transparent communication skills (verbal and written).

• Capable of working on multiple projects/tasks and able to meet timelines.

• Self-starter with a high-level of comfort with ambiguity and complexity and the ability to multi-task while consistently delivering quality results.

• Team-oriented, progressive thinker who enjoys participating in an innovative and creative work environment.

Preferred Skills:

• Experience in implementing and/or managing inventory management system.

• Working knowledge of commercial manufacturing.

• Experience developing, negotiating, and executing clinical or commercial supply and/or quality agreements.

jobs.title: Senior Accountant, e-Commerce (Contract)
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Senior Accountant – E-Commerce Accounting

Inventory • COGS • Sales • Cash Application • SAP & System Integrations

Position Summary
The consultant will support full-cycle accounting for the online store, from customer orders and inventory movement through revenue, cost of goods sold, accounts receivable, cash application, refunds, and financial reporting. This role will partner with Accounting, Operations, E-commerce, Supply Chain, and IT to resolve reconciliation and system-integration issues involving e-commerce, order management, inventory, payment, and SAP platforms.

Key Responsibilities

·       Own full-cycle accounting for online store activity, including inventory, sales, cost of goods sold, accounts receivable, cash, refunds, credits, and related balance sheet accounts.

·       Perform monthly and quarterly close activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, variance analysis, and review of transaction completeness and accuracy.

·       Reconcile inventory subledger activity to SAP, including receipts, transfers, adjustments, returns, write-offs, and inventory reserves where applicable.

·       Review and reconcile cost of goods sold to product sales and inventory movement, investigating unusual margins, timing differences, and data issues.

·       Support the complete order-to-cash cycle, including sales orders, fulfillment, billing, revenue recognition, customer receivables, refunds, credits, and cash application.

·       Reconcile payment processor and bank activity to customer orders, accounts receivable, and SAP postings; research unmatched or failed transactions.

·       Partner with Operations, E-commerce, Supply Chain, IT, and Finance teams to understand transaction flows across multiple systems and ensure accurate accounting in SAP.

·       Investigate integration issues between sales, order management, inventory/warehouse, payment, and SAP systems, and determine the accounting impact of incomplete, duplicated, delayed, or incorrect transactions.

·       Participate in system implementations, integration changes, user acceptance testing, and validation of automated accounting entries and interfaces.

·       Develop and maintain reconciliation tools and controls to confirm that data transferred between operational systems and SAP is complete and accurate.

·       Identify root causes of accounting and system issues, coordinate resolution with technical and operational teams, and help prevent recurring problems.

·       Create and maintain process documentation, system flow documentation, and internal controls for online store accounting processes.

·       Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and strengthen accounting processes as online store activity and systems evolve.

Qualifications

·       Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

·       Approximately 2–6 years of accounting experience, preferably including inventory, revenue, order-to-cash, e-commerce, retail, or consumer product accounting.

·       Strong understanding of general ledger accounting, reconciliations, month-end close, inventory accounting, revenue, accounts receivable, and cash.

·       Experience with SAP strongly preferred; experience with other large ERP systems is also valuable.

·       Experience working with e-commerce platforms, order management systems, warehouse/inventory systems, payment processors, or system integrations is a plus.

·       Strong Excel and data analysis skills, with the ability to work through large transaction populations and identify exceptions.

·       Ability to understand end-to-end transaction flows and translate operational or system issues into accounting impacts.

·       Strong problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

jobs.title: Senior Finance Manager, Product & Engineering
jobs.description:
About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Finance Manager to serve as a key partner to Mixpanel’s Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) organizations. This person will own infrastructure cost, EPD opex, and headcount planning while building scalable systems to improve visibility and decision-making, as well as the analytical frameworks that guide how Mixpanel deploys capital and allocates resources across these areas. You’ll partner cross-functionally with Engineering and Product leadership, People, and Finance to ensure investments are intentional, efficient, and aligned with long-term company strategy.

Responsibilities

• Own the Product investment envelope – Manage OpEx and headcount budgets across EPD. Ensure investments align with company strategy while maintaining efficient spend and margin targets.

• Drive rigorous workforce planning across technical and corporate teams – Build bottoms-up headcount models by function and level. Partner with Engineering leaders to sequence hiring against roadmap needs, compliance requirements, and operational scale.

• Model infrastructure and internal systems economics – Develop clear forecasting models for cloud hosting, AI/compute, internal tooling, SaaS applications, and enterprise systems. Identify optimization opportunities across both product infrastructure and corporate tech stack.

• Translate roadmap and corporate priorities into financial tradeoffs – Evaluate build vs. buy decisions, capitalizable vs. expensed R&D, and vendor investments across EPD. Provide clear recommendations grounded in ROI and long-term cost structure impact.

• Elevate budget vs. actuals rigor across the organization – Lead monthly BvA reviews for EPD. Automate reporting, improve accrual accuracy, and surface actionable insights—not just variance explanations.

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

• 8+ years of experience in FP&A or strategic finance at a high-growth technology company.

• Proven to be a partner to Engineering leaders – You’ve supported technical teams and corporate functions, understanding how product velocity and operational infrastructure translate into financial outcomes.

• Fluency in infrastructure and SaaS cost drivers – You understand cloud economics, AI/compute scaling, enterprise tooling, and how architecture and vendor decisions impact margins.

• Strong workforce planning – You’ve managed complex headcount models across multiple departments, aligning hiring pace with financial guardrails.

• Advanced financial modeling – You build scenario-driven models with clear assumptions and sensitivity analysis that stand up to executive scrutiny.

• Strong analytical judgment and the ability to identify the few variables that matter most within large and complex datasets.

• Ability to operate independently through ambiguity and bring structure to problems that do not have an established playbook.

• Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex financial and technical topics and develop polished, executive ready deliverables.

• A high say/do ratio, strong attention to detail, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where priorities, assumptions, and technology can change quickly.

Bonus Points For

• Hands-on experience with Pigment.

jobs.title: Workplace Design Manager
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is looking for a Workplace Design Manager responsible for leading the planning, design, and delivery of workplace environments that align with client business objectives, employee experience strategies, and operational requirements.

The successful candidate will combine workplace strategy, design leadership, and project delivery expertise to drive workplace transformation projects from concept development through implementation.

This is a hybrid role, 3-4 days per week, based in Menlo Park, CA.

What you'll do

• Lead workplace design projects across multiple sectors, ensuring alignment with client goals, workplace strategies, and business requirements.
• Manage the development of workplace concepts, space planning solutions, test fits, and design standards.
• Partner with clients and stakeholder groups to identify workplace needs, occupancy requirements, and future-state workplace strategies.
• Facilitate workshops, interviews, and stakeholder engagement sessions to gather project requirements and support decision-making.
• Collaborate with architects, interior designers, engineers, project managers, and external consultants throughout project lifecycles.
• Translate workplace strategy, organizational culture, and operational requirements into practical design solutions.
• Review and oversee design deliverables throughout concept, schematic, design development, and construction documentation phases.
• Ensure workplace designs support employee experience, wellbeing, collaboration, sustainability, accessibility, and inclusion objectives.
• Coordinate design activities with project schedules, budgets, and construction milestones.
• Monitor project risks, design changes, and scope impacts, providing recommendations and mitigation plans.
• Support value engineering exercises and identify opportunities to optimize cost, functionality, and user experience.
• Ensure compliance with local regulations, building codes, client standards, and industry best practices.
• Manage design consultants and vendors, reviewing performance and ensuring quality outcomes.
• Contribute to business development activities, client presentations, and workplace strategy proposals.
• Develop and maintain workplace design guidelines, standards, and best practices.
• Provide leadership, mentorship, and technical guidance to junior team members.

• Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Interior Design, Workplace Design, Environmental Design, or a related field.
• Professional registration, certification, or licensure preferred.
• 8+ years of experience in workplace design, corporate interiors, workplace strategy, architecture, or related disciplines.
• Experience managing workplace transformation, office fit-out, relocation, or corporate real estate projects.
• Strong understanding of workplace planning principles, hybrid work environments, and employee experience strategies.
• Knowledge of design development processes, construction documentation, and project delivery methodologies.
• Experience collaborating with multidisciplinary project teams and managing stakeholder relationships.
• Proficiency in workplace planning tools and design software such as AutoCAD, Revit, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar platforms.
• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
• Excellent communication, presentation, and facilitation abilities.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs*

The base salary range for this role is $150K-$160K USD. This range reflects the company's good faith estimate of the base salary for this position at the time of the posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this, we promote a healthy, productive, and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

jobs.title: Lead Photonics Validation Engineer
jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 10/17/2026

Meet the Team

The Outshift by Cisco team is one of the Cisco’s most visible innovation organizations, driving the next generation of transformative technologies and business opportunities. You will collaborate with some of the company’s most forward-thinking researchers, engineers, and technology leaders. Within the Outshift Quantum Research team and Quantum Labs, we are pioneering the design and development of practical, scalable, and efficient quantum networking technologies — foundational building blocks for the future Quantum Internet. Our multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers is dedicated to advancing the state of the art in quantum networking, distributed quantum systems, and quantum-enabled applications.

Your Impact

Cisco Quantum Research is seeking a skilled Photonic Validation Engineer to support our Quantum Experimental Team in a role that is central to the physical realization of Cisco's deployable quantum hardware platforms. You will:

• Define and implement verification protocols to validate complex photonic and electronic performance metrics (e.g., entanglement fidelity, extinction ratios, dark count rates, coincidence counts, and insertion loss) under full system integration.
• Author clear, standardized test plans, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) protocols, Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) runbooks, and detailed performance reports that give external enterprise customers absolute confidence in our delivery.
• Act as the diagnostic bridge between hardware, optics, software, and systems engineering—pinpointing root causes of inter-subsystem anomalies, cross-talk, and signal degradation to drive design iterations.
• Play a key role in establishing the assembly and test infrastructure that will support the scaling of Cisco's quantum hardware platform delivery.
• Develop comprehensive test plans, validation matrices, and automated test scripts to verify both individual subsystem specifications and full-system multi-subsystem functionality.
• Build automated data acquisition (DAQ) and instrument control setups (using Python, LabVIEW, or MATLAB) to streamline routine testing of photonic switches, detectors, laser sources, and time-tagging/coincidence electronics.
• Establish reproducible baseline benchmarks for key quantum and classical metrics, ensuring long-term operational stability and repeatability across manufacturing units.
• Perform functional and parametric testing on standalone subsystems.
• Implement integrated multi-subsystem co-validation to identify complex issues such as thermal drift, RF noise pickup, optical back-reflections, clock synchronization offsets, and control logic timing race conditions.
• Author standardized Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) execution procedures and technical sign-off criteria.
• Document, analyze, and present statistical test data, error propagation analyses, and pass/fail reports for engineering review and customer compliance packages.
• Maintain clear, traceable revision-controlled test logs, non-conformance reports (NCRs), and bug/issue tracking entries for hardware and software teams.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelors + 8 years of related experience, or Masters + 6 years of related experience, or PhD + 3 years of related experience, or equivalent related work experience.
• 2+ years of experience in test development, test automation, or hardware validation for complex optoelectronic, photonic, high-speed RF, or quantum systems.
• Experience writing code with Python or MATLAB for test automation, data analysis, and hardware instrument control.
• Experience with standard optical characterization equipment.
• Experience writing technical documentation, test protocols, FAT/SAT procedures, and validation reports.
• Experience reading, interpreting, and producing engineering drawings, schematics, and assembly procedures

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience developing electronics and control systems for lasers, electro-optic modulators, optical switches, photonic integrated circuits, or other photonic devices.

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Consultant
jobs.description:
About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Analytics Consultant. The role is essential to BOS’s shift toward an AI‑first, agentic Front Line Monitoring model, with LLMs and unstructured data analytics at the core. The role enables scalable use of LLMs, NLP, and agentic workflows to extract risk signals from qualitative data and reduce manual, judgment‑heavy processes. It provides the senior technical ownership needed to ensure explainable, auditable, and production‑ready AI adoption. Without this role, BOS faces delivery risk to its AI modernization agenda and delayed realization of signal‑quality and productivity gains already identified as strategic priorities

In this role, you will:

• Consult, review and research moderately complex business, operational, and technical challenges that require an in-depth evaluation of variable data factors
• Perform moderately complex data analysis to support and drive strategic initiatives and business needs
• Develop a deep understanding of technical systems and business processes to extract data driven insights while identifying opportunities for engineering enhancements
• Lead or participate on large cross group projects
• Mentor less experienced staff
• Collaborate and consult with peers, colleagues, external contractors, and mid-level managers to resolve issues and achieve goals
• Leverage a solid understanding of compliance and risk management requirements for supported area

Required Qualifications:

• 4+ years of Analytics experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education

Desired Qualifications:

• Advanced hands‑on expertise in Python for analytics, anomaly detection, and scalable monitoring solutions
• Practical exposure to agentic AI and LLM usage for analytics acceleration or automation
• Experience working in GCP or cloud‑based analytics platforms
• Strong SQL skills with experience handling large, complex datasets
• Solid working knowledge of SAS within risk monitoring or regulatory environments
• Strong experience designing and reviewing visualizations in Power BI, Tableau, and Python
• Proven ability to lead end‑to‑end analytical solution design and guide junior team members
• Strong understanding of data modeling, feature engineering, and analytics architecture
• Prior experience driving analytics standardization or modernization initiatives

Job Expectations:

• Applicants must be amenable to work onsite.
• Applicants must be amenable to work on mid shift and night shift
• Lead the design, delivery, and evolution of front‑line monitoring analytics to detect conduct, operational, and compliance risks across BOS. The role will own end‑to‑end risk monitoring solutions that identify trends, anomalies, and outliers, driving improvements in monitoring coverage, consistency, scalability, and timeliness.
• The individual will lead complex analytical solutioning using Python, SQL, and SAS, overseeing data preparation, metric and feature design, anomaly detection frameworks, and visualization outputs.
• The role will provide technical leadership across multiple monitoring initiatives, ensure analytical rigor, and guide effective escalation and risk insights.
• The role will play a key leadership position in BOS analytics modernization, including SAS‑to‑Python migration, adoption of GCP‑based analytics environments, and automation of monitoring workflows. In addition to hands‑on contribution where needed, the role will set analytics standards, drive documentation and reusability, review peer work, and mentor junior consultants. Exposure to agentic AI, LLM‑enabled analytics, and advanced modeling approaches is strongly preferred.
• Is critical to delivering BOS Front Line Monitoring’s 2026 mandate to drive Risk Clarity and Operational Excellence through AI‑powered analytics modernization.
• BOS has explicitly committed to transforming monitoring from rule‑centric, fragmented alerting to AI‑driven, behavioral, and trend‑based solutions, with Python, cloud (GCP), and agentic AI as the default operating model.
• This role provides the senior technical ownership required to design and scale end‑to‑end monitoring solutions, lead SAS‑to‑Python migration, automate workflows, and ensure analytics remain explainable, defensible, and audit‑ready as complexity and volume increase.
• The role also enables leverage of existing talent by setting standards, mentoring junior consultants, and operationalizing AI and agentic capabilities that BOS has identified as foundational—not optional—to how Front-Line Monitoring operates day to day.

Posting End Date:

24 Oct 2026

*Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants.

We Value Equal Opportunity

Wells Fargo is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Employees support our focus on building strong customer relationships balanced with a strong risk mitigating and compliance-driven culture which firmly establishes those disciplines as critical to the success of our customers and company. They are accountable for execution of all applicable risk programs (Credit, Market, Financial Crimes, Operational, Regulatory Compliance), which includes effectively following and adhering to applicable Wells Fargo policies and procedures, appropriately fulfilling risk and compliance obligations, timely and effective escalation and remediation of issues, and making sound risk decisions. There is emphasis on proactive monitoring, governance, risk identification and escalation, as well as making sound risk decisions commensurate with the business unit’s risk appetite and all risk and compliance program requirements.
