jobs.title: Director, Accounting
jobs.description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We’re looking for a Director, Accounting to own day-to-day accounting and treasury operations, reporting to the Controller.

The impact you’ll make:

A Mission Lane customer trusts that when they make a payment, it’s recorded right, that their balance reflects reality, and that the company behind their card is solid enough to keep showing up for them next month and the month after that. None of that happens on its own. It’s built close by close, reconciliation by reconciliation, by an accounting team getting the details exactly right. The Director, Accounting owns that foundation, keeping the numbers behind every customer’s progress ready to stand up to scrutiny.

In your first year, you’ll take full operational ownership of the day-to-day close and treasury accounting, tightening the close calendar and refining  internal  controls, audit readiness, and AI-enabled workflows toward IPO readiness demands. You’ll do that by:

• Leading the month-end close, from pre-close prep through balance sheet reconciliations and flux analysis, shrinking the calendar as you progress

• Owning the monthly consolidation across our multi-entity structure, keeping intercompany eliminations clean and GAAP compliance airtight

• Directing the annual financial statement audit as our primary external liaison, managing the PBC list and keeping the whole lifecycle on schedule

• Serving as the go-to partner for our external tax advisors and for Treasury on settlement accounting, restricted cash classifications, and reserve calculations

• Bringing AI agents into journal entries, reconciliations, and variance reporting, turning the close into something faster and sharper rather than just another deadline

• Building and developing a small, high-performing accounting team, working alongside them as a player-coach rather than directing from a distance

You’ll thrive in this role if:

• You’ve run a multi-entity close from the inside and know exactly where the friction points hide.

• You get real satisfaction from turning a messy reconciliation into a clean one, and from teaching someone else how to do the same.

• You can lead a team through real process and culture change without losing their trust, even when the change touches how they’ve worked for years.

• You see AI as a way to make your team’s work better, not a threat to it, and know how to bring skeptics along.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Active CPA and a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

• 10+ years of progressive accounting and financial management experience, including 5+ years leading a team

• Deep, hands-on experience with month-end close, financial consolidation, and GAAP compliance in a multi-entity organization

• Direct experience leading external financial statement audits end to end, including PBC management

• Working knowledge of the COSO framework and PCAOB standards related to ICFR, with experience designing and testing internal controls

• Proficiency with NetSuite or a comparable enterprise ERP, plus advanced Excel

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in financial services, consumer lending, or credit card issuing and servicing, especially with sponsor bank models, card networks, or payment processors

• Experience with Snowflake, SQL, or a BI tool like Tableau

• A track record of bringing AI or automation into accounting workflows

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $158,000 - $213,000

This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.

Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization:  nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do.

In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

Our commitment to a workplace built on respect and dignity is guided by our core value of Unity. We believe that everyone plays a vital role in our shared purpose, and we actively cultivate an environment where all individuals have the opportunity to do their best work. By fostering a culture of empathy and collaboration, we create a strong sense of belonging and support for every team member.

Mission Lane is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status.

Mission Lane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants who need them for medical or religious reasons, as required by law.  Applicants can initiate an accommodation request by contacting peopleexperience@missionlane.com.

Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters.

Application Integrity:

Our cardholders trust us with their financial well-being, and this trust starts with the integrity of the people on our team. We're looking for team members who share our dedication to transparency and truth. Please verify that the information in your application is accurate and complete.

Providing any information to Mission Lane that is not completely truthful at any point during the application or hiring process may result in removal from the hiring process, disqualification from future opportunities, withdrawal of an offer or other sanctions for candidates and, in addition for employees, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

jobs.title: Manager, Client Onboarding & Operations
jobs.description:
Twin Health

At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.

We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Guided by a dedicated clinical care team, our members have lowered their A1C below the diabetes range, achieved lasting weight loss, and reduced or even eliminated medications, all while living healthier, happier lives.

Working here

Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment.

Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® .

With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world.

Join us as we reinvent the standard of care in metabolic health.

Opportunity

We are looking for a Manager, Client Onboarding & Operations who is a self-starter energized by working with clients and building strong relationships both externally and internally to drive exceptional outcomes for our clients and members. In this role, you will own the entire onboarding and deployment of the Twin program(s) end-to-end and assist the client growth team with program management. The ability to problem solve, analyze and troubleshoot with strong verbal and written communication skills, tailored to communicate based on the situation and audience in a fast paced environment will be key.

Working with a complex clinical delivery model in a high-growth environment, our Manager, Client Onboarding & Operations has to expertly navigate through ambiguity while managing internal and external teams in a highly detail-oriented, organized and structured manner - all while ensuring we deliver on-time and exceed client expectations. As part of our small and growing team, your input and contributions will be critical to helping Twin continuously improve, optimize and scale our onboarding process.

You should be a highly organized, client-focused and a resourceful individual. This role will be a great fit for you if you are a doer who is passionate about making a difference, comfortable with ambiguity, and naturally collaborative.

Responsibilities

Drive Client Value

• Establish and maintain highly effective relationships with key stakeholders, executives and the C-suite across large enterprise clients

• Develop fluent understanding of Twin Health programs, onboarding processes, ongoing program management, growth marketing approach and clinical operations

• Successfully onboard Twin’s program(s) end-to-end across a portfolio of Twin clients, including self-insured employers, health plans and health systems

• Lead discovery sessions to gain insight into Twin’s clients’ culture, priorities, and goals in order to design tailored solutions that work for their populations

• Program manage and assist Twin’s Client Growth team with ongoing client support post-launch

• Provide consultative recommendations to increase member engagement, enhance program results, and optimize overall client satisfaction

• Perform and lead the setup, configuration, and testing of client instances to ensure proper functionality

• Coordinate internal resources and third parties/vendors for the flawless execution of projects

• Train clients on Twin programs to drive awareness and enrollment

• Analyze client data pre and post launch to provide actionable insights for internal teams and clients

Deliver Project Management Excellence

• Manage multiple complex projects simultaneously - setting expectations, managing overall project plan, and managing cross-functional teams to ensure timeliness and launch readiness

• Effectively manage client stakeholders throughout onboarding, including leading client meetings, setting and managing expectations, building stakeholder alignment, and managing risks and escalations

• Work with the clients technical leads (or 3rd parties) to operationalize data access and eligibility file management, including finalizing file/data requirements, setting up file transfer and validation, and ongoing issue resolution

• Prepare, execute and participate in special events held for or hosted by clients

• Prepare presentations and reports in a consumable client format that delivers actionable insights post launch

• Manage project expectations through regular meetings, project status reports and maintaining great relationships

• Build out standard onboarding work, templates, playbooks and internal cross-functional SOP’s to drive continuous improvement and best practice development in our approach

Lead Cross-functionally

• Manage client issues/escalations and mobilize internal teams such as Client Growth, Client Integration, Clinical Delivery, Product, Member Operations and Business Development, to drive resolution

• Work cross-functionality with teams such as Clinical Delivery, Product, Marketing, Engineering, Billing Operations and Executive teams to ensure client/market feedback is shared for ongoing improvements

• Partner with Member Marketing to develop pre-launch member promotional strategies and toolkits that will increase member engagement, enhance program results, and optimize overall client satisfaction

• Provide input and recommendations for improvements for internal processes to provide efficiency and effectiveness.

• Serve as internal team SME/point person to ensure efficiency and consistency across the onboarding lifecycle

• Drive internal alignment and manage cross-functional teams to ensure successful launches

Qualifications

• 5 - 10 years of onboarding, program management and client facing experience

• 5 - 10 years of digital health client onboarding and project management experience (manager level or above)

• Experience with health benefits, health and wellness, health plans or systems

• Ability to communicate and work across client organizations, engaging on a range of tactical and strategic issues, with senior executives as well as execution teams

• Exceptionally strong project management skills, with demonstrated organizational skills, high attention to detail and ability to balance between thoughtful planning and timely execution

• Ability to manage conflicting priorities and thrive in a fast-paced environment working under time constraints

• Proficiency with Google applications, PM tools, such as InspirePlanner, Monday.com, and MS Project

• Experience working with technical/data teams (internal and external) on data exchange, file specifications, file encryption and transmission and testing

Compensation & Benefits

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing
jobs.description:
At Evolve, we’re on a mission to make vacation rental easy for everyone. Our high-performing, customer-obsessed team runs on curiosity, communication, and accountability—working together to create exceptional experiences for our owners and guests. Whether solving big challenges, delivering outstanding results, or celebrating wins, we approach every day with purpose and passion. If you’re ready to join a mission-driven company where every teammate has the opportunity to thrive, Evolve might just be the place for you.

Why this role

As Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager, you'll own the owner lifecycle program end-to-end: the strategy, the journeys, the platform, and the results. In your first year, you'll consolidate our sending onto Customer.io, map and rebuild the journeys for each owner segment, and turn a set of disconnected sends into a measured system that drives two key metrics: qualified lead conversion and six-month owner retention. This is an owner-operator role. You'll be as comfortable building and debugging a journey in the platform and writing email copy as you are presenting strategy to leadership. We are looking for a senior individual-contributor on a small, flat team where you'll lead through clarity and evidence rather than headcount.

The team

Growth owns Evolve's owner funnel from first impression to a signed agreement and a live listing, across five programs: Attract, Convert, Launch, Nurture and Foundations. This role owns Nurture.

What you'll do

Lifecycle Strategy & Journeys

• Own owner lifecycle marketing end-to-end—every scheduled and triggered message an owner receives, from their first information request through onboarding, their first 180 days, and beyond.

• Audit all current and planned communications, converting findings into mapped, segment-specific journeys. Our Core, Plus, and Pro owners run distinct operations and require tailored engagement—Pro in particular needs a newly defined journey.

• Expand lifecycle channels beyond email and SMS. In-product nudges, push notifications, help content, and timed sales or onboarding touchpoints should all form a cohesive journey.

Platform & Infrastructure

• Lead the migration of owner communications from legacy platforms to Customer.io, establishing build standards and governance to prevent future fragmentation.

• Build segmentation and triggers based on real-time behavior and performance signals (e.g., owner actions, listing status, drop-off points) rather than fixed send calendars.

Pre-Activation Nurture & Recovery

• Manage pre-activation nurture and recovery, including post-information-request sequences, abandoned-lead recovery, re-engagement for unclosed sales leads, and targeted outbound campaigns.

• Optimize conversion across under-engaged lead segments, ensuring structured touchpoints exist long after initial contact.

Analytics & Optimization

• Drive core performance metrics, balancing lifecycle's contribution to qualified lead conversion with 180-day owner retention.

• Design and run A/B tests with a stated hypothesis and a decision attached to the result, and be clear about what you learned and what you're testing next

Cross-Functional Partnership

• Partner cross-functionally with sales, product, onboarding, support, and analytics to translate complex operational updates into clear owner communications.

What makes you a great fit

• 7+ years of experience in lifecycle, CRM, or retention marketing for consumer or prosumer audiences, with proven ownership of multi-stage journeys

• Hands-on expertise with enterprise marketing automation platforms (Customer.io, Braze, Iterable, Marketo, or similar), including building, deploying, debugging, and optimizing journeys directly

• Proven track record of accountability for revenue, conversion, or retention targets driven by lifecycle initiatives

• Experience auditing and consolidating fragmented communication systems into a single platform and coherent architecture

• Strong analytical mindset with experience segmenting audiences, analyzing cohort/journey performance, and executing hypothesis-driven A/B tests.

• Exceptional copywriting skills, with the ability to write clear, engaging, human-sounding content tailored to business owners.

• Experience marketing to small business owners or prosumer segments.

• AI-native workflow—proficiency using modern tools (e.g., Claude) to enhance research, drafting, and analysis capabilities.

Preferred but not required

• Lifecycle experience spanning pre-purchase prospect nurture through post-purchase retention.

• Familiarity with Customer Data Platforms (CDPs) and collaborating with data engineering teams on event definitions and identity resolution.

• Background in marketplaces, hospitality, travel, real estate, or financial services (short-term rental or property management experience is a plus).

• Experience managing multi-channel surfaces alongside email and SMS, including in-product messaging and push notifications.

• Basic design skills or proficiency in tools like Canva or Figma for rapid asset creation.

Compensation

For this role, compensation is based on a base salary plus a department variable annual bonus. Our base salary range is $160,000–$190,000.

Location

All Evolve team members must live in one of our approved locations by their first day. We can hire from anywhere in the U.S. except D.C. and Hawaii. Some positions may also have restrictions based on compensation in the following states: California, Maryland, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Washington. If you live in Colorado, you can work remotely anywhere in the state, at our downtown Denver office, or a hybrid of both! If you're planning to move soon, please let us know, and we'll be happy to review your application again.

California Applicant Privacy Policy | Evolve

How we reward Evolvers

We’re intentional about offering benefits that empower every Evolver to thrive both professionally and personally because they’re more than perks—they’re investments in our customer-obsessed, high-performing team.

We believe in treating others as they want to be treated, providing benefits that deliver real value, and challenging the status quo to meet the diverse needs of our team. Whether it’s helping you take care of your health, plan for the future, or celebrate life’s milestones, our offerings are designed to support you every step of the way.

• Financial Wellness: Industry-competitive pay, equity in the company, and a 401(k) with a 4% immediate vesting match.

• Family Support: 16-18 weeks of paid parental leave for birthing parents and 10 weeks for non-birthing parents, plus infertility coverage.

• Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, with 100% employer-paid dental and vision for individual coverage, a low-cost medical option, 10 free mental health visits, and pet insurance.

• Time to Recharge: Generous PTO, RTO (for full-time exempt employees), sick leave, holidays, and a personal holiday to celebrate what matters most to you.

• Travel Perks: Annual Evolve travel credit after one year and discounts on stays at all Evolve properties.

• Growth Opportunities: World-class onboarding programs, learning, and development resources to help you grow your impact.

• Connection: Employee Resource Groups celebrating our diverse communities at Evolve.

How we work together

With our core values as our guide, every Evolver helps shape the company we want to work for and the people we want to be. We’ve cultivated a culture of collaboration, care, and responsibility that we can all be proud of, and we’re excited to see what you’ll bring as your authentic self.

Still curious about who we are and what we do? Read more about our business and our culture at evolve.com.

EEO

At Evolve, we are committed to diversity and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, all qualified candidates will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, age, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), gender identity or gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, military service or veteran status, physical or mental disability, or any other legally protected characteristic. Evolve participates in e-Verify for all positions.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please let your recruiter know.

No

Demonstrated leadership presence; models Allegiant’s core values and professional standards, and sets the example for team behavior and performance.
Experience conducting performance reviews, delivering constructive feedback, and addressing performance concerns in a timely, fair, and consistent manner.
Strong work ethic and drive to achieve established goals and deadlines, with a desire and commitment to learning, growth, and continuous improvement.
Highly organized with a strong ability to multitask and a self-starter able to prioritize.
Proven ability to learn quickly and adapt to a changing environment; agile, flexible, and resilient.
Detail-oriented, professional attitude, reliable, and possesses a high degree of accuracy.
Ability to work independently and with a team in a fast-paced and high-volume environment with accuracy and timeliness.
Superior analytical and critical thinking skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and collaboratively within the organization at all levels.
Ability to present to management.
Documentation, research, and problem-solving/resolution skills.
Responsive to internal and external company needs, with a sense of urgency, accountability, a results-oriented mindset, and commitment to follow up.

Experience within the petroleum or airline industry.
Strong problem-solving skills, basic accounting principles knowledge, and data analysis skills.
Knowledge and experience in petroleum pricing, fuel supply, distribution, refining, or trading.
Ability to recommend and implement strategic courses of action relative to various fuel circumstances.
Excellent negotiation skills to appropriately advance the company’s agenda, as well as to successfully resolve commercial and/or technical disputes.
Familiarity with performance management systems, talent development frameworks, or workforce/headcount planning tools.

Lead, coach, and develop the fuel procurement/contract team; set clear individual and team goals and objectives aligned with department and company priorities.
Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, and development conversations; create individual development plans and support career growth for team members.
Monitor and manage team workload, capacity, and productivity; assess headcount and staffing needs and recommend adjustments to leadership as business needs evolve.
Establish and track team performance metrics (accuracy, timeliness, cost savings, compliance) and hold the team accountable to established standards.
Recruit, interview, and onboard new team members as needed; manage team scheduling, coverage, and workload distribution.
Foster a positive, engaged, and collaborative team environment; address performance or conduct concerns promptly, fairly, and consistently.
Model Allegiant’s core values and customer service standards in personal actions and when providing leadership direction; set the example for team behavior, collaboration, and accountability.

Manage and execute annual and ad hoc RFP processes, and implement sourcing strategies to support company goals and requirements.
Manage the process of fuel supply and service contract terminations, expirations, extensions, and renewals.

Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and controls that ensure a reliable fuel supply and limit inventory risk.
Manage ITP supplier negotiations, contract compliance, and dispute resolution.
Ensure Allegiant and affiliated airlines receive reliable, cost-effective fuel support wherever needed by the company.

Maintain relationships with fuel suppliers, transportation companies, storage operators, in-plane operators, and airports through regular communication.
Track and complete market research and analyze competitors to gauge opportunities to reduce fuel costs.
Arrange fuel releases for ad hoc charters, diversions, aircraft delivery, and maintenance.
Communicate and distribute monthly fuel nominations to all fuel supply vendors.
Work with vendors to manage the pipeline and truck schedule.
Manage, update, and distribute weekly system-wide contracted fuel pricing: Platts, Argus, and OPIS indexes.
Attend, represent, and participate in fuel consortium meetings to ensure that the airport’s fuel farm or distribution system is operated safely, efficiently, and cost-effectively.
Assist and provide support to the Fuel Invoice team with disputes and ensure timely corrections of any discrepancies.
Work with other Allegiant departments (Accounting, Quality Assurance, Safety and Training, Tax, Treasury, Accounts Payable, Airport Services, Finance, OCC, Dispatch, etc.) as needed to support fuel management and company objectives.
During fuel supply disruptions or constraints, coordinate with Fuel Inventory, OCC Dispatch, Fuel Farm Managers, carriers, and airport stakeholders to develop and execute short- and long-term mitigation plans.
Coordinate with TPSS, fuel systems, procurement systems, BI teams, external fuel vendors, and other cross-functional company initiatives impacting fuel and operations to automate and streamline manual processes, resolve system issues, and support system upgrades, regression testing, and UAT activities.
Lead coordination for internal and external audits impacting fuel contracts; serve as the primary point of contact for auditor requests and evidence gathering.
Coordinate timely responses to internal and external auditors, including documentation retrieval, control walkthroughs, process demonstrations, and remediation action plans when gaps are identified.
Maintain a strong understanding of invoice approval workflows and signature authority requirements; diagram end-to-end approval process flows, ensure adherence, and update documentation and controls as policies, systems, or roles change.
Assist in preparing fuel usage reports, cost summaries, projections, KPI dashboards, and ad-hoc reporting to support team OKRs and executive decision-making.
Other duties as assigned.

May be required to lift, push, pull, or carry up to 20 lbs. May be required to work various shifts/days in a 24-hour situation. Regular attendance is a requirement of the role. jobs.title: Branch Supervisor 2
jobs.description:
Pay Range: $74,100 - $90,800

Remote Eligible: No

We offer a pay-for-performance compensation program including bonuses for all employees and a competitive benefits package. See https://www.cuofco.org/careers for a high-level overview of our benefits package and bonus offerings.

General Purpose of the Position

This role is responsible for assisting with the direction and administration of branch operations, ensuring compliance with established policies and procedures while overseeing the delivery of exceptional member service. This role supervises a full range of services to both current and prospective members, ensuring prompt, professional, and personalized service, along with effective collaboration across departments. The Branch Supervisor acts as Branch Manager when needed, and provides training, direction, and supervision to branch staff to ensure efficient, consistent, and high-quality service. Additionally, this role performs various branch-related functions as required.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Member Service & Problem Resolution

• Answers Member Advocates’ questions, solves problems, and assists with complex transactions and sensitive member relations problems. Makes judgments for Member Advocates (within limits of authority) pertaining to all operations of branch.

• Ensures that members' requests and questions are promptly, efficiently, and courteously resolved. Explains policies and procedures to members. Answers member’s questions or refers appropriately.

• Demonstrates “escalation resolution” skills to effectively address critical member needs and concerns, recognizing and championing branch/organizational opportunities such as process improvements.

• Assists with Member Advocates functions. Performs duties related to transaction and loan processing, new account openings, account servicing including deposit products, and safe deposit boxes (if applicable). Verifies deposits, process loans, and approve transactions within established limits

• Provides excellent service by demonstrating courtesy and personal concern for members and coworkers needs and followsup to ensure those needs are met.

• Promotes branch business development and seeks to broaden member base.

• Responsible for reviewing and responding to Member Loyalty surveys in a timely manner and sharing any feedback internally as appropriate.

• Reviews and monitors the work of branch personnel. Provides suggestions to leadership and supports as necessary.

Team Leadership & Development

• Responsible for interviewing, hiring, and training Member Advocates, as well as planning, assigning, and directing work. Assists with new employee orientation and staff training sessions, ensuring employees are well-trained in all aspects of their roles.

• Ensures employees are knowledgeable about Credit Union products, services, and policies.

• Effectively cross-sells and coaches employees to offer Credit Union products and services to its members.

• Helps lead change management efforts by guiding the team through new initiatives, process updates, and organizational changes to ensure smooth transitions and continued service excellence.

• Assists with tracking individual progress, conducting performance appraisals, and formulating and implementing corrective actions as needed.

• Contributing beyond the branch by supporting and leading organizational projects.

Operations & Compliance

• Ensures Branch security. Assists with opening and closing the building in accordance with set hours. Tests security equipment as assigned.

• Supports branch and team by verifying operations are conducted in accordance with established Credit Union policies, legal and regulatory requirements, and audit standards. Provides suggestions for improved effectiveness.

• Completes required reports and records and ensures that Branch functions, internal controls, and audits are properly documented.

• Ensures that the Branch cash and transactions are in balance at the close of each day. This includes ensuring that all reports are prepared. Provide assistance to Member Advocates as needed.

• Investigates ATM and Member Service out of balance conditions and institutes corrective procedures. Assists in finding balancing errors. Ensures that each Member Advocates balances at the end of each day and secures all funds in compliance with established procedures. Maintains ATM functionality and oversees cash vault operations including ordering, balancing, resolving discrepancies, and maintaining appropriate cash levels in all cash entities. Assists with Member Advocates functions. Performs duties related to transaction and loan processing, new account openings, account servicing including deposit products, and safe deposit boxes (if applicable).

• Assists with implementing changes to established policy and procedures within the Branch.

• Assists with determining appropriate staffing levels and scheduling employees.

• Ensures that the Credit Union's professional reputation is maintained.

• Replaces Branch Manager as necessary. Assists with personnel functions and operational oversight as assigned.

• Ensures that work area is clean, secure, and well maintained.

• Required to comply with NCUA requirements and register as a Mortgage Loan Originator and keep a current registration in compliance with the SAFE Act.

• Adhere to all Federal and State laws and regulations applicable to the credit union, including the Bank Secrecy Act and OFAC.

• Responsible for compliance with the Fair and Accurate Credit Transaction Act (FACTA), the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and the Anti Money Laundering Act, including monitoring for such illegal activity as it applies to this position.

• Actively serve as a Notary Public and Medallion/Signature Guarantee for the branch.

• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other administrative officials and the public.

• Ability to apply interpersonal skills that develop member confidence, respect and trust in Credit Union of Colorado and develop cooperative relationships with all levels of people throughout the organization.

• Ability to operate related computer applications and business equipment.

• Ability to exercise good judgment and discretion in applying and interpreting credit union policies and procedures.

• Ability to turn ideas into action and quantifiable results.

• Ability to communicate and connect effectively

• Ability to inspire trust and confidence from their teams, peers, and organization

Nice-to-Haves

• Demonstrated effective leadership skills to select, motivate, develop and supervise assigned personnel.

• Understanding of all branch operations and functions.

• Understanding of credit union services and products.

• Understanding of Credit Union philosophy.

• Understanding of Credit Union’s field of membership.

• Knowledge of legal and regulatory requirements.

• Knowledge of basic accounting.

• Relevant industry experience a plus

• Strong organizational, project management, and analytical skills.

• Performs additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree or four years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

DIRECT REPORTS

Branch Member Advocates, Assistant Branch Supervisor, if applicable

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is typically required to remain stationary for long periods   and is occasionally required to lift/move or transport up to 10 pounds. Employee needs to occasionally move about inside an office to access files, mail, office machinery, etc. and constantly operates a computer and other office equipment, such as a phone, copier/printer, etc. Employee needs to position self to maintain computers, including under desks and in the server closet.  Will frequently communicates with members and co-workers and must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations . Employee will travel to visit CU location as needed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Credit Union of Colorado is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Please note applicants can redact any information that identifies their age, birth date, or dates of schooling on either their resume or any additional materials provided.

jobs.title: Senior Principal, Business Management - Debt
jobs.description:
WE’RE FINANCING THE FUTURE OF ENERGY

Crux is the capital platform for the clean economy. We modernize capital raising and deployment for clean energy and critical infrastructure with solutions across advisory, investments, technology, and intelligence.

Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.

 


AN INFLECTION POINT IN AMERICAN ENERGY AND MANUFACTURING

Energy demand is growing for the first time in decades, driving an urgent need for more affordable and reliable electricity. More electricity requires new clean energy infrastructure and strong domestic supply chains for minerals and components — as well as large amounts of capital.

Traditional project financing is opaque, fragmented, and analog. At Crux, we’re changing that. Through unmatched insights and expertise, white-glove service, purpose-built tools, and risk underwriting, we power a more prosperous, clean, and secure energy future.

We are scaling quickly and looking for team members who are eager to combine deep expertise with an AI- and tech-forward mindset.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Principal, Debt is a senior deal leader on Crux's Debt Business Management team within Capital Solutions. Reporting to the Head of Debt, the Senior Principal leads a book of debt mandates from IOI through close across Crux's three debt motions: debt origination, debt advisory, and debt attached to tax equity and preferred equity structures. The role spans the full range of debt products, including construction, term, and back-leverage facilities, tax equity and credit bridge loans, equipment financing, and green bonds and securitization.

This role requires a passion for the clean energy transition, a builder's mindset, and a commitment to delivering results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You thrive on solving complex problems and working collaboratively across teams to drive meaningful impact.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead a book of debt mandates from IOI through close as the primary negotiator and senior execution lead — driving lender diligence, structuring, negotiation, documentation, and close to institutional standards

 - Own transaction velocity and close rates across your deal book, contributing directly to the Debt team's revenue and P&L targets

 - Author credit memos and pricing recommendations and present transactions to Credit Committee, with rigorous analysis of credit quality, structural terms, risks, and mitigants

 - Lead deal teams of junior team members — staffing transactions, reviewing underwriting, diligence, and financial models, and mentoring junior team members on credit and execution

 - Run debt execution with lenders and institutional capital providers inside shared accounts, in partnership with Strategic Bank Capital and Strategic Institutional Capital

 - Partner with Industry Coverage to qualify opportunities early, take clean drivership of execution at IOI, and provide real-time market and financeability feedback that sharpens sourcing

 - Partner with Investments on the TE/preferred-equity attach motion, sourcing and pricing competitive debt within agreed turnarounds to deliver integrated capital solutions for sponsors and investors

 - Lead specific workstreams within the Head of Debt's product agenda — such as new lender programs, financing structures, or term sheet and documentation standards — in partnership with Structuring

 - Help build and standardize repeatable execution processes across debt motions, and drive adoption of AI-enabled modeling and automation across the deal lifecycle

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to define and prioritize transaction tooling that increases deal throughput and execution quality

 - Represent Crux in industry and market dialogues — webinars, whitepapers, and conferences — in coordination with coverage relationship owners


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, or related field; MBA, JD, or advanced degree a plus

 - 10-12+ years of total experience, including 7+ years in renewable energy project finance, infrastructure debt, or structured lending, with a track record of leading construction, term, back-leverage, or debt capital markets transactions as the primary negotiator

 - Deep expertise in project finance debt structures for solar, wind, and storage, including hands-on negotiation of credit agreements, intercreditor arrangements, and the interplay between tax equity and debt

 - Experience preparing and presenting transactions to credit or investment committee, ideally with perspective from both the lender and sponsor/advisory side

 - Experience leading and mentoring deal teams, including reviewing junior team members' underwriting and modeling work

 - Exceptional negotiation and relationship skills with developers, lenders, and investors, and the credibility to lead senior-level conversations

 - Strong judgment and comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-scaling environment

 - Strong interest in leveraging technology and AI to improve debt execution

 - FINRA SIE, Series 79 and 63 required or willingness to obtain under Crux's broker-dealer sponsorship


WHAT WE BRING

 - Backing, traction & brand:
   
   - We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Ardent Venture Partners, Pattern, Clearway, EDFR, Intersect, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.
   
   - $500m debt warehouse facility from Nuveen to invest in clean energy.
   
   - Have been profitable and are growing exponentially
   
   - We have closed over 120+ transactions in just the last 2 years, facilitating billions of dollars of capital flowing into renewables projects

 - Culture & working dynamic
   
   - Remote-first operating model: Work from anywhere in the US and Canada, or work out of our optional offices in DC, NYC, & SF. Optional co-working opportunities with co-workers in, Seattle, Denver, Boston, LA, and beyond.
   
   - High growth & high ownership culture: We grow quickly by giving extremely talented people a lot of responsibility.
   
   - Best of financial services & technology: We have brought together a team that are experts in clean energy finance, and the best technologies. Use your expertise while getting to be on the cutting edge of applying AI to your day and your clients’ experience.
   
   - Regular team offsites: We sustain culture by bringing the entire company together 2 times a year. Individual teams may also meet up more frequently.

 - Benefits
   
   - Healthcare: We cover 100% of premiums for employees with a variety of plans on Aetna (nationwide) and Kaiser (WA and California) and subsidize 70% for dependents (total as a group), if relevant.
   
   - Dental & vision: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and 50% for dependents (each), if relevant.
   
   - Holidays: 10 company holidays per year.
   
   - Paid time off: 20 days per year.
   
   - 401k: We support a 401k account but don't have a matching program set up at this time (typical for an early-stage startup).
   
   - Parental leave: 16 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents.

 - Compensation:
   
   - Compensation: $300,000s - $500,000s+, depending on years of exp. & revenue scope, not inclusive of equity value.
   
   - Stock options in a rapidly growing company.

 - Values
   
   - Care for each other: We want to work on a team where people support each other - in their growth, in their work, and towards our shared mission. When we do that, we have fun.
   
   - Build and improve rapidly: We move quickly. To do that, we focus, consistently ask ourselves if we are prioritizing the right things, and execute them as best as possible.
   
   - Focus unremittingly on customers: Our first obligation is to our customers and partners, and we keep their needs front and center in everything we do.
   
   - Demonstrate ownership: We are all owners of Crux. This is our team, our company, our product and we show that to each other.
   
   - Convene a team that reflects the breadth of experiences in the country: We’re building a team with a wide range of backgrounds and a culture where everyone can thrive.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Sourcing Methodology (SMO) Analyst
jobs.description:
About Cook Systems

For over 30 years, Cook Systems has partnered with organizations across the country to solve technology challenges and build strong technology teams. As a veteran-owned IT consulting company, we combine decades of industry experience with a continued focus on how technology, AI, and the way people work are evolving.

Our work spans technology consulting, talent development, and AI-enabled solutions. We value people who take ownership, adapt quickly, communicate well, and care about the quality of their work. Whether you’re early in your career or bringing years of experience, you’ll have the opportunity to keep building your skills, contribute to meaningful client work, and grow with a company that continues to evolve with the industry.

SMO (Sourcing Methodology) Analyst
Memphis, TN
Contract

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
Acts as an IT sourcing subject matter expert using the Sourcing Methodology for the planning, due diligence, contract negotiations, and governance process for IT spend. Conducts spend analysis, identifies opportunities, coordinates and collaborates with internal stakeholders on complex sourcing events and leads key initiatives.
Ensures adherence to corporate contracting standards and policies. Develops robust sourcing strategies to maximize value and minimize risk. Solicits / analyzes request for proposals; negotiates contracts and collaborates with Legal Department on contract terms and contract execution. Establish a supplier relationship management process focused on continuous improvement. Monitors market dynamics and communicate changes to internal stakeholders. Contributes to new supplier selection process and developing and maintaining supplier relationships.
Serves as the primary point of contact to assigned business units for sourcing needs.
Monitor the financial and market performance of the suppliers to identify potential supplier viability risks, communicate the risks to stakeholders and develop a risk mitigation action plan in conjunction with IT Strategy.
Look for opportunity to optimize supplier spend and value by combining, terminating or extending contracts according to organizational objectives.
Regularly review contracts with organizational stakeholders to ensure pricing models, usage, and service levels are current and optimized and that the supplier adheres to all terms and conditions.
Responsible for continuous quality, service, satisfaction and cost from suppliers to support efficient business operations.
Responsible for working with subject matter experts to gather and assess business requirements. Maintains a high degree of confidentiality specific to ITS data (including budget) and contract terms/ conditions and ITS related organization planning.

REQUIREMENTS
Must have excellent written communication skills to effectively and accurately convey detailed and complex information regarding contract specifications, policies and procedures to consultants/contractors and internal clients
3+ years of experience in IT sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or strategic sourcing.
Proven experience supporting complex sourcing events, RFP processes, and contract negotiations.
Experience working with IT vendors, technology contracts.
Prior experience supporting enterprise‑level sourcing or procurement transformation initiatives preferred.

Additional Details:

• Workplace Setting: Hybrid #LI-Hybrid

Benefits at Cook Systems

We want our employees to have benefits that support their health, financial well-being, and life outside of work. Eligible Cook Systems employees have access to a comprehensive benefits package beginning the first of the month following their hire date, including:

• Dental and vision coverage

• Life, critical illness, and accident insurance through Unum

• Flexible Spending Account and Dependent Care FSA options through Navia

• Health Gap Insurance through Sun Life

• 401(k) retirement plan through The Standard, with eligibility after six months

Beyond benefits, Cook Systems is a place where we expect people to take ownership of their work, communicate openly, continue learning, and contribute to the teams and clients they support.

We have been building technology careers and client partnerships for more than three decades, and we continue to evolve with the industry. If you’re looking for an opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your capabilities, and be part of what comes next in technology, we’d like to hear from you.

jobs.title: Quality Systems Manager
jobs.description:
We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

Provides corporate-level leadership and governance for the Gruns Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring standardized, effective, and compliant quality systems are implemented across the organization. This role establishes and maintains corporate quality system requirements, supports facility implementation and continuous improvement, and partners with facility Quality teams to ensure alignment with applicable regulatory, customer, certification, and company requirements. The Quality Systems Manager drives consistency, compliance, data integrity, training effectiveness, and inspection readiness across the organization. This role reports into the Director of Quality.

This role is part of our remote HQ! We have a fully remote, high-trust work environment - and also come together on a biannual basis for amazing off-sites where we can connect IRL.

In this role, you will:

• Owns, implements, maintains, and continuously improves the corporate Quality Management System (QMS), establishing standardized quality processes, procedures, governance, and expectations across Gruns facilities.

• Provides QMS guidance and support to facility Quality teams to ensure corporate requirements are effectively implemented, maintained, and consistently applied while allowing for site-specific procedures where appropriate.

• Manages the corporate Document Control program, including creation, review, approval, issuance, revision, periodic review, archival, obsolescence, and controlled distribution of policies, SOPs, forms, and other QMS documents.

• Manages the Change Control program and ensures proposed changes are appropriately documented, risk-assessed, reviewed, approved, implemented, communicated, and verified for effectiveness, as applicable.

• Manages and supports the corporate Food Safety and Quality Training Program, including development and maintenance of learning plans, training matrices, training assignments, completion tracking, retraining requirements, and training records in coordination with facility Quality teams.

• Serves as the business owner and primary Quality administrator for Veeva QualityOne, supporting system configuration, user adoption, workflow implementation, data integrity, reporting, and continuous improvement of electronic QMS processes.

• Develops, maintains, communicates, and supports implementation of WBC Quality Standards and other corporate Quality standards, ensuring requirements are translated into effective facility-level programs and procedures.

• Provides governance and workflow support for CAPAs, deviations, non-conformances, and Out-of-Specification (OOS) events, including documentation quality, investigation expectations, root cause analysis, action planning, approvals, effectiveness checks, trending, and timely closure.

• Manages complaint trending and quality data analysis to identify recurring issues, emerging risks, systemic trends, and opportunities for corrective, preventive, or continuous improvement actions. Communicates significant trends to Quality leadership and applicable stakeholders.

• Supports facility and corporate Management Review by compiling, analyzing, and presenting QMS performance indicators, trends, CAPA/deviation/OOS status, complaint data, audit observations, training performance, and other relevant quality metrics.

• Supports internal, customer, regulatory, and certification audits by ensuring corporate QMS documents and records are current, controlled, complete, and audit-ready and by assisting facilities with preparation, responses, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.

• Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Operations, Product, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and other applicable teams to ensure quality system requirements are incorporated into business processes, new initiatives, and organizational changes.

• Monitors QMS effectiveness through metrics, trending, periodic reviews, and compliance assessments and recommends system improvements based on identified risks, recurring issues, audit findings, and business needs.

• Provides training, coaching, and technical guidance to facility Quality teams and other stakeholders on corporate QMS processes, documentation expectations, QualityOne workflows, and applicable Quality standards.

• Ensures corporate quality records are maintained, retained, readily retrievable, and protected in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, company policies, and established record-retention requirements.

• Supports harmonization and standardization of quality systems across facilities while escalating significant compliance, product quality, or food safety risks to Quality leadership.

Basic Qualifications:

• Demonstrated experience implementing, managing, and improving Quality Management Systems (QMS) in a regulated food, dietary supplement, consumer health, or related environment.

• Working knowledge of applicable FDA requirements, including 21 CFR Part 111, and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs).

• Experience with document control, change control, training systems, CAPA, deviations, OOS investigations, complaint trending, and quality metrics.

• Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS); Veeva QualityOne experience strongly preferred.

• Knowledge of GFSI/SQF quality and food safety system requirements preferred.

• Ability to develop corporate standards and effectively support implementation across multiple facilities.

• Strong written and verbal communication, organization, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, drive timely closure of quality system activities, and influence stakeholders without direct authority.

Education:

• Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Quality, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related field with 5+ years of Quality Systems/Quality Assurance experience, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant technical work experience.

• Relevant certifications or formal training in quality systems, auditing, HACCP, SQF/GFSI, root cause analysis, or CAPA are preferred.

• Training and Experience with the 21CFR part 111

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we're committed to providing a competitive total compensation package — grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the base salary range is $125,000 - $140,000 plus bonus depending on experience, paired with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and growth of our team.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

jobs.title: Senior Recruiter, Corporate (Contract)
jobs.description:
Clover Health's mission is to improve every life. Clover Health operates as a next-generation Medicare Advantage insurer, which leverages Clover's flagship software platform, the Clover Assistant, to provide America's seniors with highly affordable, “obvious” healthcare plans. By empowering physicians with data-driven, personalized insights at the point of care through the Clover Assistant platform, Clover strives to improve clinical decision-making and outcomes.

This role sits in our People Operations team, which is at the center of three distinct lines of business: the Clover Health Medicare Advantage plan, our field-based Clinicians and Care Teams caring for our members, and Counterpart Health, our SaaS subsidiary driving adoption of our flagship software platform. This drives complexity, nuance, and highly visible opportunities for our People Team and the programs we build.

We are hiring a Contract Senior Recruiter to find and win the best talent in the market. This is a 6-month contract, fully remote, reporting to our Head of Corporate and Technical Recruiting and working closely with the CPO and our Head of Talent. You will own searches from individual contributors through director and VP level, and you will build the market intelligence behind them.

The role is designed for researchers powered by curiosity, who use AI as part of how they work.

As Clover's Senior Contract Recruiter, you will:

• Own full-cycle recruiting for People Operations & Corporate roles across levels and teams, from intake through offer.

• Build target company lists and market maps from scratch for each priority search.

• Research culture, structure, and org dynamics at target companies, and document what you learn so the next search starts further ahead.

• Go deep inside those organizations to identify the strongest people, including those who are not actively on the job market.

• Represent Clover and our story with accuracy and confidence, including the mission and the less obvious complexity of running multiple lines of business.

• Run leadership searches with retained-search rigor, using your own judgment and discretion on strategy and confidentiality.

• Direct AI tools across sourcing, research, outreach, and pipeline management, and know where they fall short.

• Partner with the Chief People Officer and Head of Recruiting on calibration, slate quality, and what raising the bar means for each role.

• Keep hiring managers and the recruiting team current on market conditions, candidate sentiment, and pipeline health.

Success in this role looks like:

• 30 Days: You have a strong grasp of our open roles, can confidently speak to the Clover story, and are building market intelligence to fuel our search strategy.

• 90 Days: You have scoped priority Corporate searches with hiring managers and calibrated with the Chief People Officer. You have built target company lists and market maps for each search and proactive outreach is underway.

• 6 Months: You have filled numerous Corporate roles, including at least one leadership search. You have put in place reusable talent maps for priority target companies and hiring managers see a higher, more defensible bar in every slate.

• Future: Market mapping and proactive sourcing are standing practice for People Operations recruiting, and the rest of the recruiting team borrows your patterns.

You should get in touch if:

• You have recruited leaders across corporate functions: You have demonstrated success filling leadership-level roles, such as directors or department heads, through in-house recruiting or agency search.

• You map the market before you call it: You have built target company lists from scratch, researched the culture and structure of each, and used that work to decide whom to approach and how.

• You find people who are not looking: Your best hires came from outreach you initiated, and you can describe how you identified and won them.

• You can tell a story that holds a skeptic: You have sold a company and a mission to a senior candidate who had never considered the industry. You can explain Medicare Advantage and a SaaS subsidiary in the same conversation.

• You have a point of view on AI: You have a preferred set of tools, a reasoned argument for them, and a clear sense of where each one fails. AI is part of how you source, research, and manage pipeline, and you still make the final call.

• You have shipped something others use: A prompt library, workflow, or research template you built that left your own desk and changed how a team works.

jobs.title: Principal, Business Management - Debt
jobs.description:
WE’RE FINANCING THE FUTURE OF ENERGY

Crux is the capital platform for the clean economy. We modernize capital raising and deployment for clean energy and critical infrastructure with solutions across advisory, investments, technology, and intelligence.

Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.

 


AN INFLECTION POINT IN AMERICAN ENERGY AND MANUFACTURING

Energy demand is growing for the first time in decades, driving an urgent need for more affordable and reliable electricity. More electricity requires new clean energy infrastructure and strong domestic supply chains for minerals and components — as well as large amounts of capital.

Traditional project financing is opaque, fragmented, and analog. At Crux, we’re changing that. Through unmatched insights and expertise, white-glove service, purpose-built tools, and risk underwriting, we power a more prosperous, clean, and secure energy future.

We are scaling quickly and looking for team members who are eager to combine deep expertise with an AI- and tech-forward mindset.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

The Principal, Debt is a senior deal leader on Crux's Debt Business Management team within Capital Solutions. Reporting to the Head of Debt, the Principal leads a book of debt mandates from IOI through close across Crux's three debt motions: debt origination, debt advisory, and debt attached to tax equity and preferred equity structures. The role spans the full range of debt products, including construction, term, and back-leverage facilities, tax equity and credit bridge loans, equipment financing, and green bonds and securitization.

This role requires a passion for the clean energy transition, a builder's mindset, and a commitment to delivering results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You thrive on solving complex problems and working collaboratively across teams to drive meaningful impact.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead a book of debt mandates from IOI through close as the primary negotiator and senior execution lead — driving lender diligence, structuring, negotiation, documentation, and close to institutional standards

 - Own transaction velocity and close rates across your deal book, contributing directly to the Debt team's revenue and P&L targets

 - Author credit memos and pricing recommendations and present transactions to Credit Committee, with rigorous analysis of credit quality, structural terms, risks, and mitigants

 - Lead deal teams of junior team members — staffing transactions, reviewing underwriting, diligence, and financial models, and mentoring junior team members on credit and execution

 - Run debt execution with lenders and institutional capital providers inside shared accounts, in partnership with Strategic Bank Capital and Strategic Institutional Capital

 - Partner with Industry Coverage to qualify opportunities early, take clean drivership of execution at IOI, and provide real-time market and financeability feedback that sharpens sourcing

 - Partner with Investments on the TE/preferred-equity attach motion, sourcing and pricing competitive debt within agreed turnarounds to deliver integrated capital solutions for sponsors and investors

 - Lead specific workstreams within the Head of Debt's product agenda — such as new lender programs, financing structures, or term sheet and documentation standards — in partnership with Structuring

 - Help build and standardize repeatable execution processes across debt motions, and drive adoption of AI-enabled modeling and automation across the deal lifecycle

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to define and prioritize transaction tooling that increases deal throughput and execution quality

 - Represent Crux in industry and market dialogues — webinars, whitepapers, and conferences — in coordination with coverage relationship owners


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, or related field; MBA, JD, or advanced degree a plus

 - 8-10+ years of total experience, including 7+ years in renewable energy project finance, infrastructure debt, or structured lending, with a track record of leading construction, term, back-leverage, or debt capital markets transactions as the primary negotiator

 - Deep expertise in project finance debt structures for solar, wind, and storage, including hands-on negotiation of credit agreements, intercreditor arrangements, and the interplay between tax equity and debt

 - Experience preparing and presenting transactions to credit or investment committee, ideally with perspective from both the lender and sponsor/advisory side

 - Experience leading and mentoring deal teams, including reviewing junior team members' underwriting and modeling work

 - Exceptional negotiation and relationship skills with developers, lenders, and investors, and the credibility to lead senior-level conversations

 - Strong judgment and comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-scaling environment

 - Strong interest in leveraging technology and AI to improve debt execution

 - FINRA SIE, Series 79 and 63 required or willingness to obtain under Crux's broker-dealer sponsorship


WHAT WE BRING

 - Backing, traction & brand:
   
   - We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Ardent Venture Partners, Pattern, Clearway, EDFR, Intersect, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.
   
   - $500m debt warehouse facility from Nuveen to invest in clean energy.
   
   - Have been profitable and are growing exponentially
   
   - We have closed over 120+ transactions in just the last 2 years, facilitating billions of dollars of capital flowing into renewables projects

 - Culture & working dynamic
   
   - Remote-first operating model: Work from anywhere in the US and Canada, or work out of our optional offices in DC, NYC, & SF. Optional co-working opportunities with co-workers in, Seattle, Denver, Boston, LA, and beyond.
   
   - High growth & high ownership culture: We grow quickly by giving extremely talented people a lot of responsibility.
   
   - Best of financial services & technology: We have brought together a team that are experts in clean energy finance, and the best technologies. Use your expertise while getting to be on the cutting edge of applying AI to your day and your clients’ experience.
   
   - Regular team offsites: We sustain culture by bringing the entire company together 2 times a year. Individual teams may also meet up more frequently.

 - Benefits
   
   - Healthcare: We cover 100% of premiums for employees with a variety of plans on Aetna (nationwide) and Kaiser (WA and California) and subsidize 70% for dependents (total as a group), if relevant.
   
   - Dental & vision: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and 50% for dependents (each), if relevant.
   
   - Holidays: 10 company holidays per year.
   
   - Paid time off: 20 days per year.
   
   - 401k: We support a 401k account but don't have a matching program set up at this time (typical for an early-stage startup).
   
   - Parental leave: 16 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents.

 - Compensation:
   
   - Compensation: $300,000s - $500,000s, depending on years of exp. & revenue scope, not inclusive of equity value.
   
   - Stock options in a rapidly growing company.

 - Values
   
   - Care for each other: We want to work on a team where people support each other - in their growth, in their work, and towards our shared mission. When we do that, we have fun.
   
   - Build and improve rapidly: We move quickly. To do that, we focus, consistently ask ourselves if we are prioritizing the right things, and execute them as best as possible.
   
   - Focus unremittingly on customers: Our first obligation is to our customers and partners, and we keep their needs front and center in everything we do.
   
   - Demonstrate ownership: We are all owners of Crux. This is our team, our company, our product and we show that to each other.
   
   - Convene a team that reflects the breadth of experiences in the country: We’re building a team with a wide range of backgrounds and a culture where everyone can thrive.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Revenue and Financial Automation
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Revenue and Financial Automation (RFA) team at Stripe is building a modern, revenue-focused, financial management platform for fast growing, digital native companies. Sub-orgs within RFA: Atlas, Business Network, Tax, Billing, and Reporting & Accounting & Data Services (RADS).

• Atlas: Atlas makes starting an internet company faster and simpler by decreasing the complexity and bundling everything you need. Founders, from anywhere in the world, can create a company, open a bank account, and be ready to charge customers, fundraise, and hire a team—in a few clicks.

• Business Network: We are building the "N" in the GPTN -- enabling businesses on Stripe to discover and conduct commerce with other businesses using cheaper faster rails.

• Tax: You know how everyone loves taxes? And it's such a simple, stable, and well-understood area? We handle all the sales-related taxes (across Checkout & Billing) and make it super easy to register, auto-collect the right amount of tax, and access the reports you need to file returns globally

• Billing: Hundreds of thousands of businesses of all sizes and types use Stripe Billing to collect revenue for recurring and one-time payments across a variety of different pricing models—from selling SaaS subscriptions, to orchestrating multi-stage contracts, delivering Usage-Based Billing, and providing recovery and retention tools to prevent customer churn.

• RADS: Building user-facing products to deliver a best-in-class analytics, data services, and reporting and analytics platform for all Stripe users.

As an engineer on the team, you’ll be responsible for shaping and building a suite of products that let our users model and operate their business more efficiently. You will work on projects that span technologies, systems, and processes where you will design, build, test, and ship great code every day. In this cross functional role, you will collaborate with experts in infrastructure, security, design, and operations to build mission critical internal and external features that power Stripe users around the world.

Responsibilities

• Design the next generation of Stripe products, to meet the high growth needs of our company and customers for years to come.

• Deliver value through a strong collaborative and users-first approach with stakeholders and customers.

• Participate in roadmap planning and prioritization.

• Debug production issues across services and several levels of the stack.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 2-12+ years of experience in software development.

• Ability to write high quality code (in programming languages like Go, Java, C/C++, etc.)

• Hands-on experience contributing to or building large scale distributed systems

• Strong collaboration skills, can work across workstreams within your team and contribute to your peers’ success

• Have the ability to thrive on a high level of autonomy, responsibility, and think of yourself as entrepreneurial

Preferred Qualifications
