YOU

 - Fast-paced experience – 2-3 internships in a top-tier role (e.g., consulting, private equity), at a high-growth startup, or you've built something of your own

 - Founder DNA – you have high agency, drive and a serious work ethic; you thrive in ambiguity and don't wait for direction, or for a process that doesn't exist yet

 - Learning at full speed – you're useful in week one and indispensable by week four

 - Competitive by nature – you've won at something hard, and losing still annoys you days later

 - Gets shit done & zero ego – you move fast, figure things out, and you'd rather ship it than get the credit

jobs.title: EHS&S Specialist
jobs.description:
About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible. Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

Sila is seeking an EH&S Specialist to join our Environmental, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS&S) team in supporting a fast-growing, 24/7 manufacturing operations site. Reporting directly to the EHS&S Site Manager, this individual contributor will play a pivotal role in developing, implementing, and continuously improving fit-for-purpose EHS&S compliance programs and risk reduction strategies.

You are a pragmatic, hands-on safety professional who thrives in a dynamic manufacturing environment. You excel at collaborating directly with cross-functional shop-floor teams ("Silazens") to establish clear safeguards, work instructions, and standards that prevent high-consequence safety and environmental events. You advocate for simplifying safety processes—making it effortless for colleagues to work safely and difficult to do work unsafely. You bring a strong continuous improvement mindset, high adaptability, and a deep commitment to protecting our workforce, environment, and surrounding community.

Responsibilities

• EHS&S Program Development & Execution: Assist in developing, updating, and supporting sitewide EHS&S policies, standards, work instructions, and training materials across critical safety domains, including Lockout/Tagout (isolation of hazardous energy), Confined Space Entry, Work at Heights, Electrical Safety, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), Waste Management, and Hot Work.

• Hazard & Exposure Assessments: Perform comprehensive chemical and equipment hazard assessments. Recommend built-in engineering, process, and equipment safety features to minimize employee exposure to physical and chemical hazards while maintaining strict regulatory compliance.

• Industrial Hygiene & Exposure Studies: Conduct employee exposure monitoring studies (noise, airborne contaminants, chemical exposures) within training and qualification limits as required.

• Incident Investigation & Root Cause Analysis: Lead and support internal inspections, audits, near-miss reporting, and incident investigations. Define robust corrective actions (CAPA) and partner with site personnel to track actions through to completion.

• Emergency Response & On-Call Support: Serve on the Sila Emergency Response Team (ERT) as Safety Officer, participating in designated on-call rotation schedules to provide off-hours site coverage and emergency support.

• Data Analytics & Continuous Improvement: Track and analyze event and near-miss trends to educate site personnel, inform safety committees, and proactively build risk-mitigation measures into site operating systems.

• Regulatory Compliance & Research: Accurately research and analyze relevant federal, state, and local regulations, codes, and industry standards to guide Sila’s ongoing compliance efforts.

• Documentation & Safety Leadership: Maintain EHS&S records, data, and compliance documentation in a consistent, audit-ready manner. Actively represent the EHS&S team across site safety committees and councils.

Core Expectations & Deliverables

• Program Simplification: Streamline existing safety procedures into easy-to-follow work instructions that integrate seamlessly into standard operating procedures for 24/7 plant shifts.

• Actionable Risk Reduction: Drive timely resolution of all open CAPA items, near-miss findings, and audit action items in collaboration with plant operations.

• Emergency Readiness: Maintain full qualification and operational readiness on the site Emergency Response Team (ERT), fulfilling designated on-call responsibilities.

• Safety Culture Stewardship: Foster a proactive, low-ego safety culture across all shifts by modeling Sila’s core values: Winning Together, Owning It, Mastering Your Craft, and Finding & Facing Facts.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Health, Chemistry, or a related science-based discipline preferred.

• Experience: Minimum of 2+ years of hands-on Environmental, Health & Safety (EH&S) program support experience within a manufacturing, chemical processing, advanced materials, or fast-paced industrial environment.

• Regulatory Knowledge: Solid foundation in OSHA, EPA, and state-level EHS regulations and standards (e.g., LOTO, Hazard Communication, Industrial Hygiene, Confined Space).

• Communication & Collaboration: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to build strong working relationships with shop-floor technicians, engineers, and executive leaders.

jobs.title: Assembly Design Kit (ADK) Engineer
jobs.description:
About SK hynix America:

At SK hynix America, we are at the forefront of semiconductor innovation. As a global leader in HBM, DRAM, and NAND flash technologies, we develop the advanced memory solutions powering everything from advanced mobile technology to massive AI data centers. With major investments in the U.S. and a leading position in the global AI revolution, we build the critical infrastructure of the digital landscape and remain committed to sustainable operations. We invite innovative minds to be part of our journey. Here, you will be part of a collaborative team pioneering the next generation of memory technologies, expanding our market footprint, and defining the future of computing.

Work Model: Onsite

Job Overview:

SK hynix America is seeking a highly experienced and motivated ADK (Assembly Design Kit) engineer to join our Advanced Packaging R&D team. In this critical role, you will be at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, leading the development of robust design rules and verification flows for our next-generation 2.5D/3D Interposer and Heterogeneous Integration technologies.

You will serve as the vital bridge between package architecture, process integration, and design implementation. Your primary responsibility will be defining the Design Rules, DRC (Design Rule Check), and LVS (Layout vs. Schematic) frameworks that ensure our advanced designs are manufactural, reliable, and high-yielding. The ideal candidate possesses deep expertise in Physical Verification (PV), a comprehensive understanding of semiconductor packaging processes (specifically TSV, Micro-bump, bridge die and RDL), and the strategic ability to translate complex process constraints into design rules. Furthermore, you will play a key role in optimizing the overall design-to-signoff flow, ensuring seamless integration across multidisciplinary teams.

Responsibilities:

• ADK Development & Maintenance: Lead the creation and maintenance of comprehensive Assembly Design Kits (ADK) tailored for advanced packaging technologies (2.5D/3D IC, SiP, Fan-Out).

• Rule Definition & Verification: Define, debug, and validate Design Rules (DRC) and Layout vs. Schematic (LVS) checks, accounting for package-specific constraints such as bump placement, RDL routing, TSV integration, and wire bonding.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with package design, process integration, and manufacturing teams to ensure design rule accuracy, maximize yield, and accelerate time-to-market.

• Physical Verification Support: Provide expert support to design teams in resolving complex physical verification issues arising from die-to-package integration and heterogeneous stacking.

• Flow Automation & Optimization: Develop and automate verification flows using advanced scripting, integrating tools from Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA to enhance efficiency and data integrity.

• Design Flow Strategy: Analyze and optimize the end-to-end package design flow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing best practices to streamline the journey from concept to GDSII sign-off.

Qualifications:

• Education: B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

• Experience: Minimum 3+ years of hands-on experience in Physical Design, CAD, or PDK/ADK development within the semiconductor or packaging industry.

• Tool Proficiency: Extensive experience with industry-standard sign-off tools from multiple vendors such as Synopsys (IC Validator, 3DICC), Cadence (PVS, Virtuoso, Integrity 3D-IC), Siemens EDA (Calibre)

• Technical Skills: Deep knowledge of design rule structures, verification methodologies, and GDSII/OASIS data formats.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Design Flow Expertise: Proven track record in managing physical design flows from concept to GDSII/OASIS sign-off. Ability to translate process constraints into design rules, whether in advanced packaging or front-end logic/foundry technologies.

• Scripting skills: Proficiency in Tcl, Perl, Python, or SKILL for flow automation is highly preferred.

• Manufacturing Insight: Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes (Reflow, Molding, Bonding or Front-end FEOL/BEOL processes) and their impact on residual stress and design rule margins.

• Excellent communication skills to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary, global R&D environment.

Benefits:

• 401k Matching

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for Health Care & Dependent Care

jobs.title: Visual Designer
jobs.description:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.


ABOUT THE ROLE

At Picogrid, design is shared infrastructure that shapes how the entire company shows up. As the company scales, we're growing our graphic identity and building systems that put our standards directly into teammates' hands.

As Visual Designer, you will apply and extend Picogrid's brand across presentations, technical diagrams, documents, hardware, and merchandise. Working closely with the Design Lead, who sets brand direction, you will help standardize brand visuals, apply them to new surfaces, and build the tools that make them easy to reproduce.

You will partner with Marketing, Engineering,, and Business Development and have real ownership over brand applications and the workflows behind them. You will be expected to make informed decisions and find creative ways to support quality at speed.

This role is ideal for a designer with strong graphic design fundamentals, who enjoys building visual identities, working in multiple mediums and is already experimenting seriously with AI-assisted production.





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Create elegant, clear graphics and communication across physical and digital surfaces

 - Develop and extend the brand system - work with the Design Lead to formalize and document brand standards, then apply them to new surfaces as the company grows

 - Develop templates for presentations, product graphics and documentation

 - Turn standards into tools that allow non-design teammates to produce high quality output

 - Build AI-assisted brand workflows - create and maintain custom instructions, skills, prompt libraries, and generation pipelines that encode our standards where teammates already work

 - Scale recurring production

 - Drive adoption across the company - find where teams produce off-brand work, give them a faster on-brand path, and train them on the tools

 - Contribute to high-profile brand and marketing campaigns

 - Maintain the foundation - organize the brand asset library and keep tools and templates current as the brand evolves




WHO YOU ARE

 - Your graphic design and typography fundamentals are strong, and your portfolio shows it

 - You think in systems. When you design one asset, you're already sketching the template, tool, or workflow that produces the next hundred.

 - You make informed decisions and explain them clearly. You push back constructively when work doesn't meet the standard.

 - You earn trust across functions. Engineers, marketers, and business development leads adopt what you build because it makes their work easier.

 - You pair craft with pragmatism. You care about the details, and you ship tools people actually use

 - You build with AI, not just use it. You've written the instructions, wired the pipeline, or scripted the template that made the output better and faster.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3–5 years of professional experience in graphic design, brand design, or visual communication

 - A portfolio that demonstrates strong graphic design and typography, including systems work: identity systems, template suites, or reusable tools

 - Proficiency in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, or other modern design tools

 - Hands-on experience building with generative AI - custom instructions or skills, generation pipelines, automated templates, or code-based design tools

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; able to explain design decisions and train teammates on new tools

 - U.S. Person status required for access to ITAR-controlled environments




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with industrial design, print, or hardware

 - Experience writing or formatting technical documentation or user guides

 - Experience designing data visualization or technical diagrams

 - Prior experience at a startup, defense technology company, or other fast-paced technical environment

 - Interest in defense, robotics, aerospace, or technically complex systems

 - Degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Industrial Design, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Picogrid is at an exciting stage where one designer cannot personally touch every piece of work. We are producing more visual assets than ever and setting the foundations for the materials produced across the company. This is where the visual designer comes in: someone equally capable of craft and systems thinking. The right person will help shape how Picogrid shows up to customers, partners, and operators as it scales.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $120,000- $160,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.

 - Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company

 - 401(k) with employer matching

 - Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)

 - Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)

 - Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 11 paid holidays per year

 - Paid parental leave for both parents

 - Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette

 - Free EV charging at the HQ

 - Unique office in El Segundo, CA stocked with quality coffee, snacks, and craft beer




EXPORT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

About Us

The Honest Company (NASDAQ: HNST) is a digitally-native consumer products company born in the Gen Z era to make purpose-driven consumer products designed for all people. Since its launch in 2012, Honest has been dedicated to creating thoughtfully formulated, safe and effective personal care, beauty, baby and household products, which are available via honest.com, third-party ecommerce partners and approximately 50,000 retail locations across the United States, Canada and Europe. Based in Los Angeles, CA, the Company's mission, to inspire everyone to love living consciously, is driven by its values of transparency, trust, sustainability and a deep sense of purpose around what matters most to its consumers: their health, their families and their homes. For more information about the Honest Standard and the company, please visit www.honest.com.

Our Mission

We're on a mission to empower people to live happy, healthy lives. We're a wellness brand with values rooted in consciousness, community, transparency, and design. Every day and in every way, we hold ourselves to an Honest standard. We believe that it is our responsibility to do our part to help create a healthy and sustainable future for all.

The Role

The Consumer Insights Data Analyst will serve as the objective source of truth on business and category performance. The ideal candidate is a curious, strategic thinker, detail oriented and a collaborative business partner who thrives in a fast-paced environment. This role owns data quality, builds the dashboards and visualizations the business runs on, and applies advanced analytics to explain performance and uncover growth opportunities, partnering cross-functionally to democratize data-driven decision making. This role is hybrid and open to either being located in Los Angeles, CA or Minneapolis, MN.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Data Analyst is responsible for duties including but not limited to the following:

• Own the source of truth: Serve as the objective, single source of truth on business performance across syndicated data sources (e.g. Circana, Stackline) and retailer POS portals. Harmonize these sources into one consistent view of consumption, share, distribution, pricing, and promotion.

• Ensure data quality and governance: Maintain data pipelines, product and retailer hierarchies, and common KPI definitions. Establish validation checks, cross-source reconciliation, and documentation to ensure data quality and accuracy.

• Report on the state of the business: Deliver weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance reporting by brand, category, channel, and retailer. Proactively flag trends, risks, and opportunities, and explain the drivers behind the results.

• Build dashboards and visualizations: Design, develop, and maintain intuitive, automated dashboards. Continuously improve usability, adoption, and refresh reliability.

• Apply advanced analytics: Lead deep-dive analyses such as sales driver decomposition, price and promotion effectiveness, distribution and velocity, assortment and share of shelf, forecasting, and incrementality. Translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.

• Democratize data: Partner with cross-functional teams (e.g. Brand, Finance, Sales, etc.) to understand business questions and key success metrics. Train and enable stakeholders to find and use data independently, building data literacy and a culture of evidence-based decision making.

• Tell the story: Synthesize data from multiple sources into concise narratives and presentations that influence strategy and unlock data-backed decision making.

• Manage data partners: Serve as the primary point of contact for data vendors (e.g. Circana) managing deliverables, database builds, and issue resolution.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

• Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years in data analytics, sales or category analytics, or business intelligence within CPG or retail.

• Education: Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative field required; an advanced degree is a plus.

• Technical Skills: Hands-on expertise with Circana, Stackline, NielsenIQ, or other retailer POS systems. Strong command of CPG measures (e.g., consumption, distribution, velocity, base vs. incremental, dollar and unit share). Advanced Excel and SQL; experience with Python or R for data manipulation and statistical modeling. Proficiency building dashboards in Power BI, Hex, Tableau, or similar BI tools. Experience with statistical methods such as regression, forecasting, and price elasticity modeling. Working knowledge of data modeling, ETL, and cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks) is preferred.

• Key Competencies: Relentless attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy and integrity. Ability to reconcile and synthesize disparate data sources into a single, trusted view. Strong business acumen and the ability to translate complex analyses into clear, actionable recommendations. Collaborative partner who can influence and educate stakeholders at all levels. Adept at managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

• Additional Skills: Excellent written, verbal, and data storytelling skills. Proactive and curious, with a drive to automate and continuously improve processes. Experience managing data vendor relationships. Passion for enabling others through data literacy and self-service tools.

Compensation

The pay range for this role is $59,000 – $74,000. Actual compensation is based on many factors including but not limited to depth of experience, skill level, ability, knowledge, education, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total rewards package for this position may also include base, annual incentive plan, benefits, retirement plan, equity, and Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Benefits & Perks

At Honest, we’re all about investing in our people. We’re dedicated to providing a benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and balance. Check out our benefits and perks we offer to help you thrive both in and out of the office:

• Comprehensive Health & Wellness 🏥: We’ve got you covered with top-tier health, dental, and vision plans to keep you and your family feeling great.

• 401k with Company Match 💰: Your future matters to us. We match your 401k contributions to help you secure a strong financial future.

• Wellness & Fitness 💪: Stay healthy with a monthly fitness reimbursement and, for those in our Playa Vista office, an onsite gym to keep you active and energized.

• Work-Life Balance ⚖️: We value your time. We provide a generous and flexible vacation policy to relax, recharge, and spend time on what matters most.

• Family-Friendly Leave 👶: Growing your family? We offer generous maternity and paternity leave to support you during this exciting journey.

• Ownership & Equity 💼: Ownership isn’t just a mindset here—it’s real. Every full time employee is granted equity, giving you a direct stake in our future. When we win, you win.

• Education Reimbursement 🎓: We’re committed to your growth—whether it’s for professional development or a new passion, we offer education reimbursement to help you learn and level up.

jobs.title: Field Installation Engineer - Region: TOLA
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION  


SPAN IS ENABLING ELECTRIFICATION FOR ALL ⚡




XFRA BY SPAN IS THE FIRST DISTRIBUTED DATA CENTER USING EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE AND UNDERUTILIZED POWER CAPACITY TO MEET EXPANDING AI COMPUTE DEMAND.



 - Decarbonization is the process to reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions, especially carbon dioxide, from entering our atmosphere.

 - Electrification is the process of replacing fossil fuel appliances that run on gas or oil with all-electric upgrades for a cleaner way to power our lives.
   
   


AT SPAN, WE BELIEVE IN:

 - Enabling homes and vehicles powered by clean energy

 - Making electrification upgrades possible

 - Building more resilient homes with reliable backup

 - Designing a flexible and distributed electrical grid





THE ROLE - THE INITIAL FOCUS WILL BE AUSTIN AND DALLAS, TX

We're hiring an XFRA Install Manager to own field installation quality, schedule, and safety across SPAN's deployment markets. You'll manage a mix of in-house electricians and licensed subcontractor crews installing SPAN Panels and XFRA outdoor compute nodes, coordinate closely with host partners and site supervisors, and be the escalation point for anything that comes up in the field — from code questions to schedule slips to safety incidents. This is a working-manager role: you'll spend real time on job sites, not just in a dashboard.




RESPONSIBILITIES

• Crew management: Manage and schedule a regional team of employed and subcontracted electricians installing SPAN Panels and XFRA nodes across job sites.

• Quality and code compliance: Own install quality across the region, ensuring every job meets NEC, local AHJ code, and SPAN's own installation standards; conduct site audits and spot-checks.

• Permitting and inspections: Coordinate permit pulls, schedule inspections with local jurisdictions, and resolve any inspection findings or code questions that come up.

• Partner relationship management: Serve as the primary field-level point of contact for partner and site superintendents, aligning install schedules with construction timelines and resolving on-site conflicts.

• Safety leadership: Own regional safety performance — lockout/tagout, arc-flash, PPE, fall protection, and general jobsite safety — including incident investigation and corrective action.

• Commissioning oversight: Ensure SPAN Panel + XFRA node pairs are properly energized, load-tested, and verified against the XFRA Secure Orchestration Layer before O&M handoff.

• Subcontractor management: Recruit, vet, and manage licensed electrical subcontractor firms, including scope negotiation, performance tracking, and onboarding to XFRA-specific procedures.

• Training: Deliver or coordinate SPAN/XFRA installation training and certification for new crews and subcontractor partners; keep training materials current as the product evolves.

• Reporting and forecasting: Track install volume, cycle time, first-pass quality, and safety metrics across the region; report up to XFRA Field Operations leadership and flag capacity or schedule risk early.

• Field escalation: Be the go-to for on-site issues — service capacity surprises, site condition problems, material shortages — and drive them to resolution.




ABOUT YOU 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Preferably, you live in Texas

• 5+ years managing electrical or low-voltage field installation crews, ideally across multiple simultaneous job sites. 10+ years general installation experience

• Background in solar, battery storage, EV charging, smart-panel systems, or similar residential electrification work; experience with a scaling or newly launched hardware product is a strong plus.

• Track record of managing subcontractor relationships, including scoping, vetting, and performance management.

• Comfort reading engineering drawings, single-line diagrams, and installation manuals, and translating them into field-ready crew guidance.

• Strong safety program experience; OSHA 30 preferred.

• Clear, structured communicator who can manage up to HQ leadership and sideways with partners at the same time.



BONUS QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience managing installs across multiple metros or with a multi-site production.

• Familiarity with utility interconnection and inspection processes across metro jurisdictions (varies significantly by AHJ).

• Experience with data-center and outdoor rack/enclosure installations.

• Prior experience standing up a new regional install program from the ground up.




LIFE AT SPAN

Headquartered in San Francisco’s vibrant SoMa neighborhood, we are an eclectic group of creative thinkers who value open communication, teamwork, and a ‘make it happen’ approach to addressing complex challenges. 

SPAN embraces diversity and equal opportunity in a serious way. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. 

We’re hiring talented individuals who are driven by success and are passionate about shaping the future of renewable energy. If that sounds like you, we’d love for you to consider joining the rapidly growing team at SPAN.



The Perks:

⚡ Competitive compensation + equity grants at a well-funded, venture-backed company

⚡ Comprehensive benefits: 100% employee premiums for base plans on medical, dental, vision with options for additional coverage.  Parental leave up to twenty four (24)  weeks depending on eligibility



Interested in joining our team? Apply today and we’ll be in touch with the next steps!

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Development & Test Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR MECHANICAL TEST ENGINEER I

Based out of Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Senior Mechanical Development & Test Engineer  II is responsible for the end-to-end design, build, test, and execution of complex internal test capabilities. This may include test setups for qualification and subsequent large-volume acceptance tests requiring high levels of automation. Hardware tests may include avionics boxes, complex mechanisms, and fully integrated spacecraft in stressing environments.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Lead qualification test campaigns.

• Lead high-volume acceptance test infrastructure development and insertion into the production floor.

• Advise on in-house test capabilities, limits, and future needs.

• Manage test projects end-to-end, to include resourcing, scheduling, and budgeting as needed.

• Hands-on work with test infrastructure implementation and validation.

• Work closely with design and other test engineers to iterate through design concepts and determine test requirements.

• Design complex Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE) to support test implementation.

QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS A SENIOR MECHANICAL TEST ENGINEER II:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline.

• 8 + years of engineering experience in the aerospace industry.

• Experience using NX Nastran, NX CAD, and Teamcenter packages.

• Experience in component and system-level environmental testing.

• Experience with test automation and post-test data analysis.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Master’s or PhD in mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline.

• Experience with Confluence and JIRA.

• Experience with Python for automation and data analysis.

• Experience leading teams of engineers and technicians.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)

$164,500—$255,275 USD

Base Salary

$132,000—$198,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

jobs.title: Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
jobs.description:
Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

US-Remote

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Who We Are

At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions provider that partners with organizations to solve meaningful challenges and drive sustainable growth. From early-stage startups to global enterprises, we work across industries to optimize our clients’ digital products through product strategy innovation, experiential design, AI solutions, and deep engineering expertise.

Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.

If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.

Who You Are

You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.

You’re highly articulate and commercially fluent. You can talk architecture with a skeptical engineering lead in one meeting and talk ROI with a client’s CEO in the next, and both walk away trusting you. You understand how technical choices shape whether a project makes money because you’ve had to make those calls yourself.

Your technical judgment comes from years of hands-on work, and you keep it current in two ways: you read widely, and you keep doing the work. “Doing” might be a few hours each week staying sharp with new tools, or it might be real delivery responsibility on a live engagement. Either way, you don’t run on knowledge that stopped accruing years ago.

You’re comfortable leading by influence rather than authority. You may not be our deepest expert on any single topic, and that’s fine, because your value shows up differently:

• You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.

• You know a good deal across a wide range of subjects and connect ideas others keep separate.

• You’re an excellent communicator, in writing and on your feet.

• You bring out people’s best work through interpersonal connection and high standards.

Your name carries some weight in the communities you’re part of. When you write or speak, senior engineers pay attention, and a few of them want to come work with you.

This is primarily a market-facing role. You’d rather be out in the market shaping where we go than waiting inside for an assignment.

What You’ll Do At 8th Light

We win work by earning technical trust before a contract is ever signed, and by being genuinely present in the market the rest of the time. This role carries both. You’ll report to the CEO and work most closely with the CEO, the VP of Growth, our practice Partners, and senior technologists.

Your primary focus will require you to:

• Join deal teams to help win new engagements. In a pitch that can mean proposing an architecture, shaping scope, sequencing the work into sensible stages, or recommending how to staff it. On our most important accounts, you’ll stay a technical presence the client trusts well after the work begins.

• Represent us and build relationships in the market. Give talks, write, and show up in person at events. In-person presence matters here, and writing alone won’t carry the role.

• Shape and sharpen what we sell. Turn what you’re seeing in the market into clearer, more current offerings, and keep our position honest: agentic products, deep platform expertise.

• Work with our Growth team to help identify and build relationships with platform and AI partners that put us in front of the right work and keep our teams current.

• Drive our go-to-market direction rather than wait for it. Bring a point of view and help us continuously iterate on where we should show up, what we should say, and which opportunities are worth chasing.

Internally, your footprint is lighter but real. You’re the standard other technologists measure themselves against, and you’re a mentor to those working on their business leadership and impact. You’ll weigh in from time to time on technical job standards and career pathing. You’ll start without direct reports and lead through influence, and as we grow, the role could grow into leading a small team.

Strongly Preferred Skills

We’d particularly like to hear from applicants with:

• A track record of pitching and winning enterprise engagements inside a consultancy

• A public technical presence: talks you’ve given, things you’ve written, communities you help lead

• Experience shaping the service offerings or the technical point of view a firm takes to market

• Relationships with cloud or AI platform partners, and the standing that comes with them

• A working grasp of where AI and agentic tooling is heading, enough to judge where the real opportunities are

• Experience mentoring senior technical talent and raising the bar around them

Compensation

Our pay range for the Field CTO role is $230,000–$287,500 USD, plus 20–30% variable compensation based on performance.

Travel Expectation

This role involves regular but not frequent travel, mostly for in-person events, client pitches, and the occasional team gatherings.

How You’ll Be Supported

At 8th Light, our culture is built on the belief that our collective growth and well-being are the drivers of our future.

• Our wellness package is designed with the Whole YOU in mind and includes:

• A robust L&D program featuring unlimited access to thousands of books, courses, and expert-led training on the O'Reilly learning platform.

• Annual financial stipend and time allotment for learning & development

• Coworking support for our global team

• Flexible PTO with floating company holidays

• 12 weeks of new parent leave available for eligible employees

See our full list of Benefits.

8th Light Hubs and Geographies

8th Light’s culture is rooted in strong connections that extend across our teams, regions, and beyond client work. We are a distributed team across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with hubs in Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle.

If you are hired into a hub, you will be part of a team with regular rituals around co-working and community building. For team members outside of those cities, we offer access to coworking spaces to foster continued collaboration and connection across our global team.

We hope to see you apply!

#LI-Remote

A Note on Your Privacy

At 8th Light, one of our core values is Honesty that builds trust — and that shapes how we approach hiring. We want you to have a clear picture of who we are, what we're looking for, and how we handle your information throughout the process.

Before submitting your application, please take a moment to review our Global Candidate Privacy Notice. By applying, you acknowledge that you've read it.

jobs.title: Prediction Markets Operations Intern (Winter 2027)
jobs.description:
About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Marketing

The Prediction Markets Operations team turns real-world events into clearly defined event contracts. We support markets across their full lifecycle—from an initial idea, through configuration and launch, into live operations, and finally to accurate resolution. Our work sits at the intersection of current events, marketplaces, and regulated products, and it demands precision at every step.

The team is responsible for making sure every contract is: clearly and objectively written, based on reliable, authoritative resolution sources, accurately configured, supported with appropriate images and content, thoroughly reviewed before launch, monitored while live, and resolved accurately and consistently.

The Role: Prediction Markets Operations Intern

This is a detail-oriented, hands-on internship for someone interested in marketplaces, operations, current events, financial technology, or regulated products. You will perform time-sensitive operational work and learn firsthand how prediction markets move from an idea to a live and, ultimately, settled contract.

Success in this role depends on accuracy, sound judgment, reliability, and operational discipline. Just as important is the willingness to escalate uncertainty rather than guess. You will support, coordinate, research, prepare, review, and execute work under established procedures, working closely with partners across Prediction Markets, Operations, Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, Design, Marketing, and our liquidity partners.

This will be a semester long internship program with 3 days a week in person at our New York City, NY office from January to April 2027.

Responsibilities:

Contract Research and Market Listings

• Research potential prediction-market contract ideas.

• Help turn ideas into precise, objective binary questions.

• Identify reliable and authoritative public resolution sources.

• Flag ambiguity, potentially prohibited subject matter, or questions requiring Compliance or Legal review.

• Prepare contract specifications, including outcomes, dates, descriptions, tickers, resolution criteria, and other listing details.

• Create and configure event contracts in the Contract Management System, or assist with structured CSV uploads, under established procedures.

• Support research and documentation related to product requirements and filings.

Quality Assurance and Launch Operations

• Perform pre-launch and post-upload quality assurance.

• Verify contract names, outcomes, ordering, start times, expiration times, resolution criteria, and designated sources.

• Review dates and times carefully, including UTC-based fields.

• Compare contracts with relevant external prediction markets when appropriate, and identify unintended differences in outcomes, timing, or mechanics.

• Confirm that event and social images are present and appropriate.

• Upload or update approved event images, social images, and display settings.

• Coordinate launch information with internal stakeholders and liquidity partners.

• Identify discrepancies and escalate issues before launch.

Customer and Live-Market Support

• Review, triage, and investigate prediction-market support tickets.

• Gather relevant facts, document findings, and route issues appropriately.

• Monitor live markets for incorrect content, timing discrepancies, operational issues, or unexpected behavior.

• Follow established incident-escalation procedures when urgent technical or operational issues arise.

• Maintain accurate trackers, checklists, SOPs, and internal documentation.

• Identify opportunities to improve repetitive workflows and reduce manual work.

Market Monitoring and Resolution

• Monitor contracts approaching expiration or awaiting resolution.

• Research outcomes using the contract’s designated resolution source.

• Prepare a proposed outcome, source links, and a concise rationale for internal review.

• Double-check resolution information against authoritative sources.

• Escalate unclear, conflicting, delayed, or incomplete source information rather than guessing.

• Execute approved market settlements in the Contract Management System after required training, review, and approval. Settlement activity is performed only under established procedures, supervision, access controls, and approval requirements. Accuracy is critical, because completed settlements may not be reversible.

• Document completed resolutions according to team procedures.

Scheduled Monitoring Coverage

• Participate in a scheduled rotation for brief evening or weekend monitoring.

• This is lightweight, scheduled coverage—not continuous or unrestricted on-call work.

• Interns will primarily identify and escalate issues to the appropriate full-time team.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Associate’s, or Master’s degree.

• Exceptional attention to detail.

• Strong written communication.

• Ability to research information and distinguish authoritative sources from unreliable ones.

• Sound judgment and a willingness to escalate uncertainty.

• Comfort with detailed, repeatable, process-driven tasks.

• Ability to manage time-sensitive work without sacrificing accuracy.

• Dependability and follow-through.

• Basic proficiency with spreadsheets and web-based business tools.

• Ability to work in-office.

• Availability for the scheduled, lightweight evening or weekend monitoring rotation.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Internship, academic, or project experience in operations, customer support, research, quality assurance, content operations, marketplaces, fintech, or another detail-oriented environment.

• Familiarity with prediction markets, financial markets, sports, politics, economics, or major current events.

• Experience with ticketing platforms, content-management systems, administrative tools, dashboards, or structured data entry.

• Interest in regulated products or operational risk.

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR MECHANICAL ENGINEER II

Based onsite at Rocket Lab Robotics in Pasadena, California, the Senior Mechanical Engineer II will lead mechanical design and mechanism development efforts for space robotics, precision mechanisms, electromechanical assemblies, tooling, fixtures, and ground support equipment. The role translates program, production, and test needs into practical mechanical architectures and drives approved designs through analysis, review, procurement, assembly, integration, environmental test, qualification, and flight delivery. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical leader with deep experience in SolidWorks, precision mechanical design, mechanisms, tolerance analysis, manufacturability, and spaceflight hardware delivery.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO

• Lead assigned mechanical and mechanism development efforts, including definition of scope, requirements, schedules, technical risks, project milestones, and verification plans.

• Serve as responsible engineer for complex components or subsystems and own technical execution through design, procurement, build, test, qualification, and delivery.

• Lead trade studies and technical decisions involving mechanical architecture, packaging, interfaces, tolerance strategy, materials, fabrication approach, assembly flow, inspection planning, verification, and design risk.

• Lead design, manufacturing, and test reviews with engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and test stakeholders; document actions and drive closure.

• Manage technical schedules, vendors, budgets, build priorities, and risk-mitigation activities needed to meet program commitments.

• Mentor less-experienced engineers and contribute to mechanical design standards, best practices, design-for-manufacture improvements, and lessons learned.

• Develop precision mechanisms, robotic systems, electromechanical assemblies, tooling, fixtures, and ground support equipment for spaceflight and ground applications.

• Translate program, system, production, and test needs into practical mechanical architectures, interfaces, packaging concepts, and verification approaches.

• Develop mechanical hardware through concept development, trade studies, detailed design, analysis, drawing release, procurement, assembly, integration, environmental test, qualification, and delivery.

• Design space mechanisms and motion systems including actuators, gimbals, gear trains, harmonic drives, bearings, motors, rotary sensors, springs, launch locks, release devices, and kinematic or pseudo-kinematic interfaces.

• Create and maintain product definition in SolidWorks, including 3D CAD models, production drawings, interface details, bills of material, assembly documentation, test procedures, and supporting design analyses.

• Apply GD&T, tolerance stack-up analysis, material and process selection, first-principles calculations, and finite element analysis to make sound design decisions.

• Design hardware for stiffness, strength, thermal environments, vibration and shock, tolerance control, manufacturability, inspectability, assembly, integration, and test.

• Work closely with electrical, software, systems, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and test teams to evaluate alternatives and deliver practical, build-ready solutions.

• •Support hardware assembly, integration, troubleshooting, inspection, environmental testing, qualification testing, fixture development, and review of test data.

• Coordinate with machine shops and suppliers to resolve fabrication questions, evaluate manufacturing approaches, and support timely hardware delivery.

• Document technical decisions, design analyses, test results, risks, and verification evidence in support of program milestones and design reviews.

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, mechatronics, robotics, or another related engineering discipline.

• 8+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience, including significant aerospace, spaceflight, robotics, or other high-reliability hardware development experience.

• 3+ years serving as a responsible engineer or technical lead for mechanical component or subsystem development.

• Proven experience delivering hardware from concept through detailed design, procurement, build, integration, environmental test, qualification, and delivery.

• Deep experience designing precision mechanisms, robotic systems, aerospace hardware, or electromechanical assemblies.

• Strong SolidWorks experience, including complex CAD modeling, production drawings, GD&T, tolerance analysis, bills of material, and mechanical design documentation.

• Experience using first-principles calculations, tolerance analysis, FEA, inspection data, and test results to guide design decisions.

• Strong knowledge of aerospace materials, fabrication processes, mechanical interfaces, environmental requirements, verification methods, and design-for-manufacture principles.

• Hands-on experience supporting assembly, integration, troubleshooting, inspection, environmental testing, qualification, and design iteration.

• Experience leading technical reviews, coordinating cross-functional teams, communicating status and risks, and mentoring other engineers.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE

• Master's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, mechatronics, robotics, or another related engineering discipline.

• Direct experience with robotic manipulators, in-space servicing, planetary robotics, precision spacecraft mechanisms, or satellite deployment systems.

• Experience designing motorized mechanisms, actuators, gimbals, gear trains, harmonic drives, bearings, rotary sensors, launch locks, release devices, or kinematic interfaces.

• Experience with structural, vibration, thermal, or thermal-elastic analysis and interpretation of environmental test data.

• Experience with NASA, JPL, DoD, commercial space, or prime-contractor flight programs.

• Experience with AS9100, configuration management, root-cause investigation, failure analysis, nonconformance disposition, or test-anomaly resolution.

• Exceptional mechanical problem-solving, technical communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)

$164,500—$233,275 USD

Base Salary

$132,000—$176,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

jobs.title: Risk Advisory - IT Risk Associate Director
jobs.description:
In today’s dynamic environment, business leaders face constantly shifting risks. Riveron helps organizations implement leading governance, risk and compliance practices by combining deep expertise with pragmatic partnership, using a hands-on approach to understand the specific needs of the organization and create tailored solutions to address key compliance risks.  

 

Our Risk Advisory services include SOX readiness, managed internal controls testing and monitoring, co-sourced/outsourced internal audit, segregation of duties and access risk review, policy and procedure development, enterprise risk management, and IT and cybersecurity risk assessment.  

 

The Associate Director position for Riveron’s IT Risk Advisory group will be the day-to-day lead for consulting engagements working collaboratively with senior team members who provide guidance, coaching, and direction. Associate Directors are expected to conduct the majority of day-to-day project management activities on all of their engagements, including project plan development, reviewing staff work for quality, status updates to clients and internal management, and mentoring of staff and senior consultants. 

Who You Are:

 - Bachelor's and/or Master’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Management Information Systems, or another relevant field

 - Relevant certification preferred, such as CISA, CISSP, CISM, CGEIT, or CIPP; CPA or is also valued but not required

 - Minimum 8 years working as IT auditor or IT risk advisor for a public accounting firm, or other operational roles with a focus on information technology compliance. Experience should include performing internal or external IT audits

 - Demonstrated knowledge of IT risk management, general and application controls, cybersecurity principles, and regulatory frameworks such as SOX, NIST, or ISO

 - You have a passion for developing and maintaining client relationships

 - You get the job done and have fun doing it

 - You communicate skillfully with a variety of audiences and can create compelling stories from data

 - You thrive in an ever-changing, dynamic work environment

 - You readily identify problems and instinctively look for solutions

 - You enjoy participating in internal and external company initiatives such as community service, training, recruiting, and firm events

 - You have the ability and desire to travel as required based on client location



What You’ll Do:  

 - Gain an understanding of the assigned clients’ business objectives, IT environment, and applicable regulatory and risk management landscape

 - Lead projects in the areas of IT General Controls (ITGC) assessments, Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) IT compliance, ERP/application control reviews, and cybersecurity risk assessments

 - Leverage knowledge of industry-specific systems, applications, and infrastructure to identify technology risks and evaluate their impact on business and financial reporting

 - Assess the design and operating effectiveness of IT controls related to access management, change management, system operations, and data integrity

 - Obtain and analyze system-generated data, configurations, and logs as a basis for evaluating control environments and identifying gaps

 - Demonstrate proficiency in developing IT control process flows, risk/control matrices, and testing strategies for general and automated application controls

 - Maintain the level of technical competency and professional care required for the completion of assignments in accordance with COSO, COBIT, and ISO auditing standards and related control techniques

 - Set priorities, ensuring daily coordination among the project team, and monitor progress against schedules, budgets, project/task deliverables and status reporting

 - Plan, review, and provide direction for the work of Staff and Senior Consultants

 - Communicate extensively with clients to drive expectations and report on the status of ongoing projects

 - Deliver oral and written presentations during and at the conclusion of projects by either recommending improvements or any operational/financial deficiencies to executive leadership

 - Stay abreast of emerging risk areas, IT trends, and related control techniques

jobs.title: Automation Engineer II
jobs.description:
At Amyris, we value that everyone’s career journey is unique and authentic to who they are. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply and grow alongside us! You may be just the right candidate for this or other open roles.

Ready to put your hands-on laboratory automation experience to work while growing your programming skills?

Join Amyris as an Automation Engineer II and help scientists work faster and more reliably by supporting, troubleshooting, and improving automated laboratory workflows. You’ll work directly with liquid handlers, laboratory instrumentation, scientists, and experienced automation engineers to develop reliable, high-throughput workflows—from genetic design through screening and analysis.

If you enjoy solving practical hardware and workflow challenges and want to build your scripting and programming capabilities, this is an opportunity to make a visible impact on a production-scale synthetic biology platform.

*This is a fully onsite role based in Emeryville, CA.

Responsibilities

• Method & Workflow Development: Support the development, modification, testing, and deployment of automated laboratory methods on liquid handlers and other laboratory automation platforms. Execute defined method-development activities independently and work with more experienced automation engineers on complex or integrated workflows.

• Laboratory Workflow Automation: Work with automation engineers, scientists, and laboratory users to understand manual laboratory protocols and help translate them into reliable automated workflows using established platforms, standards, and development practices.

• Troubleshooting & Technical Support: Provide day-to-day support for laboratory automation systems. Troubleshoot routine to moderately complex issues involving instrumentation, automation software, labware, consumables, and liquid-handling methods. Escalate complex, unfamiliar, or cross-system issues when additional technical expertise is required.

• Maintenance & Vendor Coordination: Support routine instrument maintenance, calibration, equipment qualification activities, and troubleshooting. Coordinate with equipment vendors and service providers as needed under established support processes.

• Documentation: Develop and maintain method documentation, standard operating procedures, user guides, troubleshooting instructions, and other technical documentation using established team standards.

• Continuous Improvement: Contribute to identifying operational bottlenecks, recurring automation issues, and opportunities to improve system reliability, assay execution, and automation uptime. Participate in implementation and testing of improvement efforts.

• Team Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing: Participate in technical discussions, share troubleshooting findings, seek input when appropriate, and collaborate with automation engineers, scientists, laboratory staff, vendors, and other cross-functional partners.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, a related scientific or engineering field, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience.

• Approximately 2–3 years of relevant experience in laboratory automation, laboratory instrumentation, engineering, biotechnology, pharmaceutical development, or a related technical environment.

• Hands-on experience operating, supporting, programming, or troubleshooting automated laboratory instrumentation. Experience with liquid-handling platforms is strongly preferred. (e.g., Beckman Coulter Biomek, Labcyte/Beckman Echo, Agilent VPrep, Dynamic Devices Lynx).

• Exposure to laboratory scheduling or orchestration platforms such as Biosero Green Button Go, Agilent VWorks, HighRes Cellario, or similar systems.

• Basic familiarity with scripting or programming concepts used in automation environments, such as Python, C#, VBScript, or similar languages, with an interest in developing these skills further.

• Ability to apply systematic troubleshooting methods to routine and moderately complex hardware, software, labware, and workflow-related problems.

• Ability to communicate technical information clearly, document work effectively, collaborate with laboratory users and engineering colleagues, and seek guidance when appropriate.

• Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies, incorporate feedback, and develop increasing technical independence over time.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting automation hardware, including electronics troubleshooting and repair.

• Interest or experience in mechanical troubleshooting, CAD, 3D printing, fabrication, electronics, or development of simple laboratory fixtures is a plus.

• Familiarity with standard molecular biology and synthetic biology workflows (e.g., PCR setup, DNA assembly, transformations, NGS library prep, microplate assays, or cell culture plating).

• Exposure to laboratory data systems, LIMS, file-based data exchange, or automated transfer of instrument and workflow data.

• Familiarity with Git or another version-control system for scripts, configuration files, or automation methods.

jobs.title: Senior Propulsion Structural Analyst, Integrated Design
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Propulsion team at Relativity is focused on developing and delivering highly performant and manufacturable engines for Terran R. Engineers are responsible for the entire lifecycle of their parts, from initial design through production to qualification and flight. The team fosters a culture of bottoms-up decision-making, free from technical gatekeeping, where ownership and accountability are key at all levels. But designing engines with a quarter million pounds of thrust is just the beginning. As the flight configuration enters qualification, the team is now exploring modifications for future engines, including thrust upgrades, new cycles, and design for mass production.

About the Role:

• Responsible for the thermal, structural, dynamic, and durability (fatigue/fracture) analyses on Aeon-R engines and subsystems, to guide design decisions and ensure reliability and performance requirements are met

• Responsible for the analysis of 3D-printed engine components, complex mechanical assemblies, and/or the structural integrity of the fully integrated engine assembly

• Work hand-in-hand with mechanical designers and manufacturing engineers to arrive at optimal solutions for the engine and vehicle programs

• Develop and execute tests to support development and qualification, including hands-on work like test article integration, instrumentation setup, and data processing

About You:

• Bachelor's degree in a science, engineering, technology, or mathematics field

• 5+ years of relevant Industry experience, preferably with complex engineering systems

• Experience with Finite Element Analysis

• Experience with computer aided design (CAD) software

• Detail-oriented, organized, and able to follow through

• Strong drive to deliver on ambitious schedules

Nice to haves, but not required:

• Experience with design of liquid propulsion components and systems

• Experience with Siemens NX, Teamcenter, and ANSYS workbench

• Familiarity with industry best practices

• Familiarity with aerospace standards

At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

For more than 50+ years Crestwood has been committed to creating innovative recovery programs and developing compassionate communities that support each client in their journey.  Our model of care focuses on a personal and self-directed process that empowers the people we serve and helps them to develop the skills to thrive!

Title: Mobile Crisis LVN

Job Duties: The Mobile Crisis LVN ensures we are providing safe, effective, and compassionate responses to individuals during a mental health crisis. You’ll work across content acquisition, processing, and delivery systems, ensuring high-quality outputs for both domestic and international clients while improving efficiency through automation.

• Identify opportunities to improve workflow efficiency, scalability, and accuracy

How success will be measured in this role:

• Successful transition of manual workflows into reliable automated systems

• Accuracy and quality of content processing and delivery aligned with client briefs

• Reduction in operational inefficiencies and manual intervention

• Timely resolution of workflow and system-related issues

• Clear and consistent documentation of workflows and configurations

• Effective collaboration with internal stakeholders and vendor partners

If the details below describe you, you could be a great fit for this role:

• Interest in workflow automation, systems configuration, or operational tooling

• Familiarity with automation platforms (e.g., N8N) or similar workflow tools

• Strong analytical mindset with attention to detail in system setup and monitoring

• Ability to clearly document processes and communicate across technical and non-technical teams
