jobs.title: The Safety Basis and Unreviewed Safety Question (USQ) Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

As part of the Regulations & Safety organization, Configuration Management maintains the integrity and traceability of technical information throughout the product lifecycle. The team ensures controlled changes, accurate documentation, and consistent configuration across programs.

The Role

The Safety Basis and Unreviewed Safety Question (USQ) Coordinator coordinates the safety case for Valar Atomics' operating reactor facility, interfacing daily with the design, licensing, and safety analysis teams: the analysis that proves the plant can be operated safely, and the process that keeps every design change, test, and operating discovery honest against it. The role runs the Unreviewed Safety Question process end to end, from intake to approval to regulator submittal, leads the response when an operating discovery challenges the analysis, and is the single point where design intent, licensing commitments, and safety analysis meet. Done well, this makes change control fast because it is trusted, and gives each new reactor a safety case it inherits rather than rebuilds. The role suits someone from nuclear or another high consequence regulated industry who wants ownership of a critical process and can hold a conservative line under schedule pressure. This position will be located in Torrance, California, with regular presence at the reactor site in Orangeville, UT.

The Safety Basis and USQ Coordinator will report to the Director of Licensing Documentation and Technical Publishing and be assigned to work with Facility Design Authority and Operations Manager.

Key Responsibilities

• Coordinate the plant safety analysis and technical safety requirements with the design, licensing, and safety analysis teams, and keep them current as the design and the plant evolve

• Run the Unreviewed Safety Question process: screenings, determinations, approvals, records, deadlines, and regulator submittals

• Lead the evaluation and reporting of discovered conditions that may challenge the safety analysis

• Ensure every design change is screened for safety basis impact before it is implemented

• Support the safety case for new reactor designs and its traceability to design requirements

• Qualify and train USQ evaluators and build a team that can carry the process across multiple reactors

• Be the technical point of contact to the regulator on safety basis matters

• Improve the safety basis process so each successive reactor is licensed faster than the last

Basic Qualifications

• 4+ years of experience in safety analysis, licensing, safety basis, change control, or safety engineering in nuclear or another high consequence regulated industry such as aerospace, defense, chemical, or oil and gas

• Understanding of how a safety case is built, approved, maintained, and changed

• Ability to run a controlled, deadline driven process and coordinate across engineering teams with minimal supervision

• Sound judgment and the confidence to make conservative calls under schedule pressure

• Strong technical writing and communication skills

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in engineering or a physical science

• Experience with nuclear safety analysis, Unreviewed Safety Question evaluation, or an equivalent change evaluation process

• Experience working with a regulator or authorization authority

• Experience with change control or configuration management in a regulated environment

• Experience preparing safety or licensing documents for a new facility

• Experience with requirements and lifecycle management tools (Polarion, DOORS, Jama, etc.)

What We Offer

• Competitive base salary

• Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company

• Comprehensive medical benefits

• Unlimited PTO

• Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite

• Generous PPE stipend

• High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy

• Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement

• Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders

• The opportunity to help build and scale transformative energy technology from the ground up

jobs.title: Clinical Care Pharmacist Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

Strive Pharmacy is a personalized compounding pharmacy built on a simple conviction: medicine should fit the patient, not the other way around. We started Strive because we believed the pharmaceutical industry was overdue for a more human approach—one that prioritizes individualized care, clinical nuance, and genuine partnership with patients and providers.

Compounding gives us the tools to do that. Every formulation we prepare is built to the specific needs of a specific person, and every interaction we have is guided by that same commitment to personalized care.

We're growing, and we're looking for people who share that conviction. If you're ready to be part of a pharmacy that takes the work seriously and the people even more seriously, we'd like to meet you.

Mission:

Strive exists to disrupt an industry long overdue for a more personal approach to care. We put the human element at the center of everything: every formulation, every patient interaction, every provider partnership. We're not just a compounding pharmacy. We're a team on a mission to change what personalized healthcare looks and feels like.

Position Type: Full-Time

Position Overview:

The Clinical Care Pharmacist Manager leads the Clinical Care Supervisor and Trainer team, ensuring the department delivers accurate, compliant, and clinically sound service to patients and providers. This role owns the strategic and operational health of the clinical care function—identifying process gaps, developing solutions in partnership with other department leaders, and driving those solutions through the supervisor team to the frontline. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable thinking several steps ahead on process strategy and rolling up their sleeves to make sure a change actually lands with the team.

Key Responsibilities:

• Team Leadership Manage and develop Clinical Care Supervisors and the Trainer, setting clear expectations, providing regular coaching, and building leadership capability within the team. Foster a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement across the clinical care function. Conduct regular 1:1s with direct reports focused on both performance and professional growth.

• Strategic Process Improvement Identify recurring process, workflow, and quality issues by analyzing performance data, escalation trends, and supervisor feedback; diagnose root causes rather than one-off fixes. Think strategically about long-term solutions to operational and clinical process challenges, weighing tradeoffs across quality, compliance, staffing, and patient/provider experience. Own process and SOP improvement initiatives from idea through implementation.

• Cross-Departmental Partnership Partner with leaders in Operations, Workforce Management, Compliance, and Training to bring clinical perspective into broader operational decisions, and to bring operational reality into clinical process design. Represent the clinical care team in cross-functional problem-solving discussions, ensuring solutions work in practice, not just on paper. Collaborate with Workforce Management and Operations leadership on staffing, scheduling, and service-level strategy.

• Execution & Change Management Translate strategic decisions into clear, actionable plans that supervisors can execute with their teams. Work with supervisors to determine the most effective way to disseminate process changes downstream, tailoring the approach to the team and the change. Get creative with how change is communicated—the goal is understanding and adoption, not just notification. Stay connected with the broader clinical care team, not just supervisors, to gather real-time feedback on how changes are landing, and adjust course as needed.

• Quality, Compliance & Clinical Escalation Serve as the escalation point for the most complex clinical or process-related issues supervisors bring forward. Ensure the department maintains adherence to SOPs, pharmacy regulations, and quality standards. Champion a culture of proactive reporting and continuous improvement, particularly around patient safety, medication errors, and adverse events.

• Documentation & Training Oversight Oversee the development and maintenance of training and process documentation, in partnership with the Trainer, to ensure consistency across the team. Provide clinical and frontline input into policy and SOP development.

• Active Arizona Pharmacist License

• Experience with pharmacy operations and clinical decision-making

• Proficiency in call center tools, pharmacy management systems, and workforce management software

Preferred Qualifications:

• 3+ years of leadership experience in a pharmacy or call center setting, including experience leading through other leaders (managing supervisors, not just individual contributors)

• Demonstrated strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to translate data and trends into actionable process improvements

• Strong track record of cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management

• Skilled in change management and communication, with the ability to build buy-in and drive adoption of new processes

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Empathetic leadership and conflict resolution abilities

Work Environment:

This position is primarily based in an onsite work environment. The role requires regular periods of sitting, standing, and computer use, with occasional lifting as needed. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities.

Join Us in Making an Impact:

At Strive, the work is real and the impact is direct. Every role here contributes to a patient experience that's more personal, more attentive, and more human than what most people have come to expect from a pharmacy. Apply today and help us raise the bar.

We're committed to supporting the personal and professional growth of every employee, both inside and outside the workplace.

• Scaled Content Delivery: Plan and execute webinars and scaled content assets that deepen adoption and drive customer engagement, coordinating across Marketing and CS to align with overall strategy.

jobs.title: Fleet Integration Manager, Surface Maritime
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Fleet Integration Manager to join our maritime team.
This is a dual-hatted role: you will perform test engineering duties and lead fleet integration efforts,
bringing hands-on at-sea operating experience into both. You will work closely with program leadership
and across engineering, operations, and business development to build a team focused on solving hard
problems and changing the industry. Join our team and help build the next generation of surface
platforms that redefine maritime operations.

Our team conducts full system-level development testing, new production acceptance testing,
sub-component qualification testing, and more. If it involves test, we support it. If you want to work
in an innovative, fast-paced environment where your work directly shapes the products we field, this is
a fantastic opportunity.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Testing and fleet integration are the same problem seen from two angles. A test plan written without
fleet operating experience misses the failure modes, workflows, and edge cases that matter at sea. In
this role, you’ll apply that experience directly: time spent operating unmanned or manned surface vessels
in real conditions, translated into test plans, demonstration events, and exercises that reflect how the
fleet actually operates.

You also serve as the bridge between the engineering team and the fleet. You identify gaps between our
platforms and existing fleet procedures, equipment, and concepts of employment, and feed that insight
back into design and test planning. You represent the operator's perspective in design reviews and
requirements discussions, and support direct engagement with fleet units and customers during
integration, test, and demonstration events.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Support the integration of surface platform subsystems, including sensors, navigation, propulsion, communication systems, autonomy software, and power systems, into a complete surface platform

• Develop, review, and execute test plans for development, integration, and acceptance testing, informed by hands-on fleet operating experience

• Support day-to-day test operations, including pre-mission testing, launch and recovery, vehicle tasking, and data analysis for internal and customer-facing efforts

• Design test and demonstration scenarios that reflect real fleet operating conditions, procedures, and tactics

• Identify gaps between platform capability and existing fleet equipment, procedures, and concepts of employment, and feed findings back to engineering and program leadership

• Support hands-on troubleshooting, repair, operation, and maintenance of surface maritime platforms in the field

• Author and/or review detailed test reports documenting internal and customer-facing test and evaluation efforts

• Support local and offshore sea testing and operations, including multi-day offshore operations

• Set up, collect, and refine operational metrics for test and fleet performance

• Participate in design reviews, requirements analysis, and system verification planning, representing the operator's perspective

• Collaborate with fleet units, external partners, and customers during integration and test, cataloging their requirements and supporting payload and system integration into the overall mission lifecycle

• Support configuration control, version control, documentation, and safety processes across land- and sea-based test and integration efforts, including extended hours as required

• Ability to travel up to 50% of the time, including multi-day offshore operations, with potential for more during key test campaigns and fleet integration events

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience operating unmanned or manned surface vessels at sea, with demonstrated ability to translate that experience into realistic test and demonstration scenarios, ideally as a recent Surface Warfare Officer (SWO) in the United States Navy

• Familiarity with concepts of mechanical engineering, software development and testing, electrical engineering, and control theory

• Experience in field test and/or operationally focused environments

• Knowledge of electronics troubleshooting and ability to use basic test equipment

• Proficient in reading and understanding engineering drawings and specifications

• Extremely organized and detail-oriented

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, effective across technical and non-technical audiences

• A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture

• High ownership and a bias toward action

• Ability to travel up to 50% of your time, with potential for more during key test campaigns and fleet integration events

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

• In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience integrating surface and airborne sensors, surface vessel navigation, and communication systems

• A genuine interest and 5+ years of experience in systems engineering, integration, and test

• Experience generating TRRs, test plans, test procedures, and test reports

• Demonstrated experience with marine operational procedures and equipment, spanning coastal to deep-water operations

• Experience briefing customers, partners, or fleet stakeholders on emerging capabilities

• Proficiency in data analysis tools: Python, MATLAB, R, SQL

• Experience developing and managing a test and evaluation program

• Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Benefits

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: Finance and Operations Specialist
jobs.description:
Work at Blissway: Opportunity for Impact Every Day 🚀✨

Blissway is a startup that simplifies toll collection and dramatically improves highway safety. We are multiple startups in one: Deep Tech, AI/ML, Hardware, SaaS, and IoT. For the past five years, we have built a nearly insurmountable technological lead in tolling, an industry that is quietly bigger than football. While our competitors have thousands of employees, we operate with a lean but growing team of less than 30. We’ve stayed under the radar, but our impact is visible on the massive Interstate Highway System connecting every major US metro (except Juneau, AK—sorry, Juneau).

You are a good fit if...

You have drive: You take extreme ownership. If a number doesn't tie out, you find out why. If a process is missing, you build it. We are outcomes focused, not hours focused. You know when month end, a payroll deadline, or an insurance renewal calls for an extra push.

You think clearly: You cut through noise. You can look at a P&L, a bank feed, or an aging report, spot what's wrong, decide what to fix first, and explain why it matters.

You communicate clearly: In writing and in person, you get to the point. Founders, employees, customers, and vendors always know where things stand: what's been paid, what's owed, and what's due next.

You spot and flag gaps proactively: You don't wait to be asked. You spot the lapsing insurance policy, the under-billed contract, the filing coming due, or the cash crunch three months out, and you raise it early with a recommendation.

You see finance as a system: You treat the books, payroll, and billing as a system you can build, not a pile of tasks. You automate what repeats, document the rest, and set up controls so the same mistake can't happen twice. "We've always done it this way" bothers you.

You are detail obsessed: You juggle payroll cycles, vendor payments, customer invoices, filings, and renewals at once, and nothing falls through the cracks. Every account reconciles, every deadline is on a calendar, and every invoice goes out on time.

You learn fast: You may have closed the books before, or you may have studied accounting and be ready to own it. Either way, you pick up new systems quickly, ask the right questions, and don't need to be shown twice.

You have technical foundations: You don't need to be an engineer, but you're curious about how our products work and how we make money from them. You're comfortable with automations, integrations, and AI tools, and you'd rather build a workflow than repeat a task.

Bonus points: Experience billing public agencies or government contracts (milestone invoicing, required backup documentation, long payment cycles). A CPA or progress toward one is a plus, not a requirement.



This might be you if...

You want your work to make a difference every day. You're drawn to the pace of a startup and the stability of a profitable business with long-term contracts. You love getting things done, and you'd rather own finance and operations end to end than one slice of it at a big company. You're excited to build the systems we'll scale on.



The Mission

Our technology runs on some of the busiest toll roads in the country, and our growth depends on a tight, well-run business behind it. You will own the financial and operational engine that keeps Blissway running: the logistics, deadlines, and details that let the rest of the team build. This is an individual contributor role reporting directly to our founder and CEO. You'll also partner with our outside CPA firm on tax and year-end work.

 - Keep Things Running: Handle vendor onboarding, contract records, and the day-to-day logistics that keep the company moving, and fix any process that's slowing the team down.

 - Report and Flag: Deliver monthly reporting to the founders with budget vs. actuals and a cash forecast. Flag gaps, risks, and opportunities before anyone asks.

 - Bill and Collect: Invoice customers accurately and on time, including milestone and contract-based billing for public agency customers. Follow up on receivables until they're paid.

 - Pay and Track: Pay vendors on time with clear approvals, track and categorize company spending, and keep vendor records clean, including W-9s and 1099s.

 - Close the Books: Own the monthly close: bank and card reconciliations, accruals, and a clean P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow on a predictable schedule.

 - Handle the Small Contracts: Own Blissway's non-tolling agreements from draft to signature to renewal. That covers leases (like the private road we use for testing), vendor and service agreements, NDAs, and the many small contracts a growing company signs. Negotiate standard terms, bring in outside counsel when a deal needs it, and track obligations and renewal dates so nothing auto-renews or lapses by surprise. Tolling and agency contracts stay with the founders.

 - Run Payroll and Benefits: Run payroll in Rippling and keep payroll tax filings current. Manage our ICHRA allowance, 401(k), and life and disability coverage. Manage Colorado FAMLI premiums and coordinate leave alongside our parental leave policy.

 - Protect the Company: Own business insurance renewals and certificates of insurance for customers. Keep a compliance calendar of filings, registrations, and renewals so nothing lapses.

The Essentials (Health & Wealth)

 - Relocation Support: We are excited for you to join the team at our engineering office in Denver. We value in-person collaboration and daily team lunches and we provide a relocation bonus to help you get here.

 - Personalized Health Coverage (ICHRA): We don’t believe in one-size-fits-all healthcare. We provide a monthly allowance for you and dependents so you can choose the individual plan that actually fits your life.

 - Investing in Your Future: 401(k) matching up to 4%.

 - Peace of Mind: Transparent compensation. Company-sponsored life & disability insurance.

 - Early Stage Equity: Competitive equity package. Every year, we facilitate a tender process that gives you the opportunity to sell your vested shares at the same valuation as our investors.

Rest & Recharge 🌴

 - High-Trust Time Off: 4 weeks of untracked PTO. We don't micromanage your calendar; we focus on your impact. Take the time you need to stay sharp and inspired.

 - Family First: 12 weeks of paid parental leave for birth and adoptive parents. We want you present for the moments that matter most.

 - The Deep Breath (Sabbatical): Every 5 years, take 12 weeks of fully paid leave. Go travel, write a book, or master a new hobby—then come back and tell us all about it.

Fuel & Community 😀

 - The Blissway Kitchen: Whether it’s breakfast to start your day or our daily group lunches, we keep the team fueled.

 - Snacks Autonomy: Our kitchen is fully stocked and we mean it—if we’re missing your favorite fuel, just add it to the request list.

 - The "BlissTrip": An annual 4-day getaway for the team and significant others.

 - Monthly Beats: Game nights, escape rooms, and dinners to celebrate the grit we put in.

 - Continuous Learning: Tuition reimbursement for courses, programs, and conferences that sharpen your craft.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Robotic Applications
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is ushering in a new era of micromanufacturing with its Matter Compiler™ technology platform. This platform enables new classes of micromachines to be designed and built by providing manufacturing processes and a materials library that are inaccessible to semiconductor manufacturing methods. It unlocks MEMS manufacturing not only for device classes that could never be produced by semiconductor methods, but also for entirely new categories. Furthermore, this digital platform is fully programmable in the way 3D printing is digital—but whereas 3D printing produces parts of a single material using a single process, the Matter Compiler™ technology platform is a multi-process, multi-material system: bits and raw materials go in, and complete, functional micromachines come out. The Atomic Machines team has also created an exciting first device—made possible only through the Matter Compiler™ technology platform—that we will be unveiling to the world soon.

Our offices are in Emeryville and Santa Clara, California.

About The Role:

Our manufacturing system is composed of nodes; each delivers a unit of manufacturing capacity for a process, and there are a dozen or more node types. As a Software Engineer, Robotic Applications, you will bring nodes to life: designing the automation sequences, state machines, and APIs that turn integrated hardware into reliable, repeatable manufacturing capacity. Your deliverable is software, mainly Python, in the application layers of our stack: the APIs that wrap a node to automate manufacturing processes, the orchestration that sequences motion, vision, and process steps for throughput, and the calibration and diagnostic tooling that lets us replicate nodes and keep them healthy.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with mechanical, electrical, and process engineers through bring-up: one week defining machine behavior with a mechanical designer, the next chasing cycle time out of a motion sequence or root-causing a failure that crosses the software/hardware boundary. You can try code on the machine in the morning and land it as a tested, typed package through CI in the afternoon.

What You’ll Do:

• Design and implement machine behavior: automation sequencing, state machines, failure detection and recovery, and the APIs that expose it all.

• Write code that makes unsafe commands impossible rather than merely discouraged: enforce invariants, validate before touching hardware, and leave the machine in a known state on every exit path.

• Ship a simulator or mock with every device, test sequencing, timing, and recovery without the machine, and extend the conformance suite every machine runs in CI.

• Optimize cycle time: instrument sequences, find where time goes, and overlap or restructure motion/vision/process steps to get it back.

• Bring up new hardware with cross-functional teams, and build the calibration, verification, and diagnostic tools that make the next copy of a machine faster to stand up.

• Debug across the stack: from a misbehaving sensor or homing failure up through orchestration logic, using logs, telemetry, and the machine itself.

• Contribute to system reliability through observability that shows a machine degrading before it stops, fault handling, and graceful recovery, so machines run without babysitting.

• Take a turn on the on-call rotation: periodically a one-week shift that includes the weekend (about once every 10 weeks; less frequently as the company grows and eventually transitioning to dedicated support teams). Current coverage slots are 6am–2pm or 2pm–10pm, and you will not be expected to work beyond the shift for those days.

What You’ll Need:

• 3+ years developing software for systems that interact with hardware or the physical world (level set by experience and interview performance; we hire L3–L5 on this posting).

• Depth on something you built: at least one system you can take us two layers down into, what you wrote, why that design, what broke, and how you found it.

• Strong programming fundamentals and fluent Python: you will write and debug Python every day, and every coding exercise in our interview is in Python. If your strongest language is something else, you are welcome if you can work in Python live; it does not need to be polished.

• A first-principles mindset: you reason about why a design works, not just how you've seen it done.

• Practical understanding of state machines, sequencing, and failure modes in systems where software drives physical hardware: what is legal from the current state, what must still hold when a step fails halfway, and why an operation that may be retried must be safe to repeat.

• Systematic debugging habits, starting from the symptom and reaching the mechanism, and the collaboration skills to chase problems across the software/electrical/mechanical boundary.

• BS in CS, EE, ME, Mechatronics, Robotics, or equivalent experience.

Bonus Points For:

• Experience bringing up and integrating electromechanical systems (sensors, actuators, motion axes) in production environments.

• Working fluency in a systems language (C++, Rust, Go); our motion stack is C++ and it helps to read it.

• Robotics depth where this job uses it: kinematics, motion planning, vision-based alignment, calibration (hand-eye, kinematic, galvo scan-field), and a track record of landing it in shipped systems.

• Experience with hardware-in-the-loop test design, observability, or simulation and digital-twin validation beyond unit-level mocks.

• Realtime or embedded experience (valuable on adjacent teams; not required here).

The compensation for this position also includes equity and benefits.

Salary Range

$170,000—$220,000 USD

jobs.title: Vice President, Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
The opportunity:

Making robotic surgery accessible to every patient starts with exceptional people. As Intuitive grows globally, the Vice President, Talent Acquisition will help us attract and hire the talent to advance that ambition—and build a TA organization ready to deliver at greater scale.

We’re looking for someone who takes the time to understand the business and its people, earns trust through honest conversations and follow-through, and brings fresh perspective to how we work. A leader who listens closely, challenges thoughtfully, and gives people a clear reason to embrace change.

Working closely with executives, Finance, and HR, you’ll help shape the talent decisions behind our growth. You’ll build on the team’s strengths while making the changes needed to simplify hiring, strengthen our global capabilities, and deliver consistently across markets.

What you’ll lead:

This individual must be passionate about building a strong team in support of a great company.  We’re looking for a leader who is deeply curious about the business, builds trusted relationships across teams and across regions, and sees opportunities to rethink how we attract and hire talent globally. Someone who brings fresh perspectives, turns ideas into results, and inspires a global team to do its best work. This is an opportunity to shape the future of TA at a defining moment in Intuitive’s growth.

What this looks like:

• Shape talent strategy with the business. Engage executives and our HR function early in business planning. Translate growth priorities into a multi-year talent acquisition strategy, bringing informed advice on talent availability, location, and hiring trade-offs.
• Connect workforce plans to delivery. Build a regular planning rhythm with Finance, the business, and HR that aligns hiring priorities, timing, investment, and recruiting capacity. Own global hiring performance and the TA budget, making commitments clear and addressing gaps early.
• Build a truly global function. Strengthen regional leadership and recruiting capabilities, particularly outside the US. Involve regional teams in designing shared systems and processes so they work across markets, with clear accountability and room for local judgment.
• Bring fresh thinking to how we hire. Question processes that add work without adding value. Introduce technology, automation, and new approaches where they improve hiring outcomes, and help teams adopt changes that make a lasting difference.
• Make data meaningful. Bring together hiring performance, talent market intelligence, and workforce trends to explain what’s changing, why it matters, and what we should do next. Help leaders use those insights to make better decisions about priorities, investment, and risk.
• Develop an exceptional team. Give leaders and recruiters clear direction, meaningful development, and the support to become trusted talent advisors. Invite different perspectives, coach candidly, and follow through on commitments. Lead change in a way that helps people understand the purpose and take ownership of the outcome.
• Lead as one HR team. Work closely with HR Business Leaders and Partners and Centers of Excellence—including Talent Management, Total Rewards, People Analytics, People Services, and Inclusion & Diversity—to solve talent challenges together. Connect hiring with broader talent priorities and share accountability for an inclusive, effective hiring experience and compliant practices across markets.

What you’ll bring:

• Global TA leadership at scale: 15+ years of demonstrated TA leadership experience, including 10+ years leading people and managing TA leaders across regions. This is a role where that global depth truly matters. This is a centralized, global function with significant growth ahead, and you've been here before: scaling TA functions through periods of rapid growth, building and leading recruiting across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas, and standing up teams in new markets from the ground up. You understand what it takes to hire effectively in diverse geographies — local labor markets, regulatory environments, cultural nuances in candidate experience, and how to design shared systems that actually work across regions without sacrificing local judgment. Ideally, you've lived or worked in-region, not just managed from headquarters — giving you firsthand perspective on what global recruiting really requires on the ground.
• Industry depth: Background recruiting in hardware manufacturing, technology manufacturing, or similarly complex, highly technical environments desired — with a strong grasp of the talent landscape, competitive dynamics, and specialized hiring challenges those industries demand.
• Talent magnet: A reputation for building organizations and employer brands that top talent wants to join. You know how to position a company compellingly in competitive markets and create candidate experiences that convert.
• Deep partnership and influence: A highly collaborative approach, with the credibility to advise executives and build strong partnerships with Finance, HR Business Leaders and Partners, and Centers of Excellence to deliver shared outcomes.
• Exceptional people leadership and team development: An open, transparent style that builds trust across cultures. You invest deeply in developing strong leaders, create clear expectations and accountability, and leave teams meaningfully better than you found them.
• Problem solving and business judgment: A natural problem solver who cuts through complexity, connects the dots across competing priorities, and brings practical, high-impact solutions. Strong business and HR acumen, with the ability to translate data into a clear story — connecting insights to business priorities, investment decisions, and action.
• Innovation and operational results: Demonstrated success modernizing TA through technology, automation, and simpler processes, while managing competing priorities and delivering measurable improvements in hiring quality, speed, and cost.

jobs.title: Director, Account Services
jobs.description:
Want to be a bswifter?

At bswift we’ve been transforming benefits administration since 1996, making it simpler, smarter, and more human. Our state-of-the-art, cloud-based technology and services empower employees to understand, manage, and love their benefits. From downtown Chicago, and remotely across the country, we serve thousands of companies and millions of people nationwide, reducing administrative burdens and freeing HR teams to focus on creating thriving, people-first workplaces.

We’re looking for motivated and goal-driven individuals who share our passion for delivering excellence and creating solutions that make a difference. The reward is a fun, flexible and creative environment with ample opportunity for professional and personal growth. If you love the bswift values of pursue excellence, embrace accountability, deliver superior service, and be a great place to work, we want to hear from you!

ABOUT US:

bswift is a leading benefits administration company that specializes in providing tailored solutions for our clients. Our mission is to simplify the complex world of employee benefits and deliver exceptional service to our clients. We are looking for a talented and experienced individual to join our Engagement Solutions team as the Director, Account Services.

bswift Engagement Solutions is our communication agency, a team of more than 50 strategists, writers, designers, researchers and communication experts who help HR, benefits and internal communications leaders create communication employees actually notice, understand and act on. We support annual enrollment, year-round benefits engagement, total rewards, benefits education and workforce communication, taking clients from research and strategy through creative development and multichannel execution. Our work has earned recognition including Gold Hermes Creative Awards, and our account management team is the engine behind it. They are the people who keep complex, high-stakes client campaigns moving on time and on point.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Director, Account Services leads the account management function within the bswift Communication Agency. This is a newly created role, built to bring structure, consistency and strategic leadership to a team that sits at the center of how our clients experience bswift.

Reporting to the Vice President, Engagement Solutions, you will lead and develop a team of account managers, own the standards and processes by which client work moves through the agency, and serve as the team’s strongest advocate. You will partner closely with the Senior Directors, Communication and collaborate with our Creative and Operations teams to ensure account managers are set up to deliver exceptional, on-time work.

We are looking for a leader who is energized by building something. You will inherit a talented team and a real opportunity to move the function from tactical execution toward proactive, strategic partnership — refining workflows, getting more out of the tools we already have, and staying at the forefront of how AI can make project management smarter and faster.

WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR (Essential Functions):

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Team leadership and development

Lead, coach and develop a team of six account managers, including regular one-on-ones, goal setting, performance reviews and career development planning

Hire, onboard and train new account managers, building ramp plans that bring new team members to full productivity quickly

Serve as a visible advocate for the account management team — surfacing capacity concerns, removing roadblocks and ensuring the team has the tools, information and support needed to do their jobs well

Balance workload and resourcing across the team, matching account manager capacity and strengths to client needs

Establish clear expectations, competency standards and career paths for the account management function

Build a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement

Client and account oversight

Own the overall health of the agency’s client relationships from an account management standpoint, ensuring consistency and quality across all accounts

Directly manage a small volume of high visibility and revenue accounts within the business, implementing account and project management best practices and leading the team through the day to day.

Set and enforce best practices for client management, including communication cadence, status reporting, escalation paths and documentation standards

Step in on complex, high-visibility or at-risk accounts to provide senior-level support, issue resolution and direct client engagement

Partner with the Senior Directors of Communication to align account management support with client strategy and consulting priorities

Identify opportunities to strengthen and expand client relationships, partnering with consulting leads to execute

Represent the account management perspective in client planning, renewal and new business conversations as needed

Project management, process and operations

Own and continuously refine the agency’s project management standards, intake processes and workflows

Ensure projects across the team are scoped, scheduled, resourced and delivered on time and within budget

Maximize the capability of the agency’s project management platform (including Monday.com), driving consistent adoption, meaningful reporting and automation wherever possible

Establish clear visibility into team capacity, project status and delivery metrics, and report on them to leadership

Partner with Creative and Operations to streamline handoffs, reduce rework and eliminate low-value manual steps

Move the function from reactive and tactical toward proactive and strategic by anticipating client needs and building repeatable approaches

Innovation and AI enablement

Stay at the forefront of AI and emerging tools in project and account management, identifying, piloting and scaling the applications that improve speed, quality and consistency

Bring new ideas to how the agency works, building the business case and leading change management for adoption

Champion continuous improvement, using team feedback and delivery data to prioritize the changes that matter most

Cross-functional collaboration

Report to the Vice President, Engagement Solutions, providing regular updates on team performance, capacity, risks and opportunities

Collaborate with the Creative, Operations, Consulting, Client Service and Implementation teams to ensure coordination, visibility and knowledge sharing on behalf of clients

Serve as a connective point between account management and the broader bswift organization

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED (Required Education and Experience):

Ten or more years of experience in project management, account management or client services, including at least two to three years directly managing and developing people

Demonstrated success leading teams that deliver complex, multi-stakeholder client projects on time and within budget

Deep knowledge of client management best practices, with the judgment to know when to standardize and when to flex

Proven ability to design and implement processes and workflows that measurably improve efficiency and quality

Hands-on experience with workflow and project management platforms such as Monday.com, including building boards, automations and reporting

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the presence to engage senior client stakeholders and internal executives

Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail and problem-solving skills

Demonstrated ability to advocate for a team while holding it to a high standard

Strong time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines across multiple accounts and competing priorities

Ability to function well in a fast-paced and at times high-pressure environment

Proficiency with the Microsoft suite, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Teams

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience

NICE TO HAVE (Preferred education and experience):

Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Advertising, Journalism, English or Business

Experience in employee benefits, HR communication or employee engagement

Prior agency or consulting experience, preferably in a leadership capacity

Practical experience applying AI tools to project management, content workflows or team productivity

Experience standing up or maturing an account management or client services function, including processes, templates and standards

Experience managing print and digital vendor relationships, and working in SharePoint

Familiarity with benefits administration technology or the broader benefits ecosystem

OTHER DUTIES

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Why Join bswift?

At bswift, we empower our employees to make a meaningful impact, innovate, and grow. Joining our team means stepping into a collaborative and dynamic environment that values creativity, initiative, and a passion for client success. We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace that celebrates diversity and values each team member’s unique contributions.

Make an Impact: At bswift, your work directly contributes to transforming how organizations approach benefits administration and client engagement. Join us to be part of an organization that is making a meaningful difference in the lives of our clients and their employees.

bswift has been regularly named one of Chicago’s Best and Brightest Companies to Work For®, as well as one of the Nation’s Best and Brightest Companies to Work For® year after year. We offer a fun, flexible, and creative environment where you can grow both professionally and personally.

jobs.description:
Powerhouse Arts (PHA) is a not-for-profit organization committed to creative expression. Located in a purpose-built facility in Brooklyn, PHA convenes an extended network of art and fabrication professionals and educators who co-create and share artistic practices vital to the well-being of artists and the communities to which they belong. PHA offers fabrication programs in ceramics, print, and public art; alongside membership studios in ceramics and at MGC Community Print Studio, textile workshop, The Alpha Workshops; and spaces for education, events, and public engagement.

Powerhouse Arts is a not-for-profit organization committed to creative expression. Housed in a purpose- built-facility in Brooklyn, the organization hosts an extended network of art and fabrication professionals and educators who work together to co-create and share artistic practices vital to the well-being of artists and the communities to which they serve. Our facilities house fabrication services, production services, production spaces, and member workshops for artisans. In 2025, PHA has welcomed in thousands of patrons as the building becomes a center for art and performance.

As the organization continues to grow and expand its impact, Powerhouse is seeking an Executive Assistant to provide executive, high-level administrative support to the President, and the Sr. Vice President. This role with provide support including calendar management for internal and external meetings, board and committee coordination and ad hoc support for events, and communications. The ideal candidate will be highly organized, detail-oriented, an excellent communicator, and will be enthusiastic about Powerhouse’s mission.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Provide high-level administrative support to the President and Sr. Vice President with daily administrative duties.

• Manage complex calendars, scheduling meetings, appointments, and complex and detailed travel arrangements and itineraries, while proactively identifying and addressing scheduling conflicts.

• Participate in planning meetings with the President and liaise with other staff, gathering and sharing information on behalf of and with the President, taking notes, and tracking follow-up action items and staff assignments

• Field all internal and external requests for meetings with the President and Vice President.

• Coordinate board meetings, draft agendas, prepare presentations, and ensure the President and Vice President are prepared with relevant material and information in advance of meetings.

• Maintain President’s contacts and update institutional databases; ensure regular upkeep of information, including data clean-up, address updates, and other data entry as necessary.

• Assist with Executive and board projects, including preparing presentations for meetings, speaking engagements, and other meeting materials.

• When needed and appropriate, facilitate sharing of materials between staff and other departments.

• Handle administrative details independently, while exercising good judgment in keeping the President and team members adequately informed.

• On special occasions order lunch for guests of the executive team, ensuring conference rooms are ready for guest with refreshments

• Greets guests of the leadership team, escorting them to meeting locations

• Gives tours of the workshops and event spaces to guests, as needed

• Support exhibitions team with admin support, including preparing loan letters, maintaining exhibition checklists, and coordinating correspondence with artists and external partners.

• Coordinate and manage business card orders, as needed

• Manage special projects as assigned by the executive team

Board Liaison:

• Act as main liaison for board members, facilitating organization of quarterly meeting scheduling, and communicating special board member details and needs to President and Development Director

• Provide administrative and strategic support regarding Board matters; schedule and attend all Board Meetings, prepare minutes and agendas, note and track follow-up action items.

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of board items and data; edit narratives explaining the scope of work of Board Resolutions.

• Maintain discretion and confidentiality regarding all Board and Executive Committee Members.

• Establish excellent working relationships with the Chairman and Members of the Board of Directors in verbal, written, and electronic correspondence

Qualifications
Powerhouse Arts is a safe, inclusive workplace for people of all backgrounds and walks of life. We strongly encourage you to apply if you are from a marginalized or underrepresented group. The
requirements listed are guidelines, you don't have to satisfy every requirement or meet every qualification listed. If 80% of what you read fits you, or if you have skills that are transferable, please
apply.

• Minimum of 5–8 years of administrative assistant experience, including 2+ years supporting senior executive leaders within a fast-paced nonprofit organization; an arts background is a plus.

• Highly organized and detail-oriented

• Proactive problem solver and communicator

• Solid written and verbal communication skills; excellent proofreading skills

• Significant experience writing and editing correspondence

• Demonstrated initiative and flexibility working both independently and as a member of a team, an accountable self-starter

• Flexible, creative, organized, thorough, and resourceful

• Fluent in G Suite, Microsoft Office Suite, Mac, and Dropbox platforms

• Comfortable using and/or learning communication and project management tools such as Asana, Zoom and Slack

• Previous experience supporting senior executives and managing complex calendars is preferred, as well as the ability to work well under pressure in a busy and dynamic environment

jobs.title: Director of Global Communications
jobs.description:
Strider Technologies delivers strategic intelligence that helps organizations make faster, more confident decisions in an increasingly complex global environment. Using cutting-edge AI and proprietary methodologies, we transform open-source data into actionable insights that help protect technology, talent, and supply chains from nation-state risks.




SUMMARY

Strider is seeking an experienced Director of Global Communications to lead and scale our corporate communications function. This role will shape how Strider tells its story to clients, partners, media, team members, and the broader market—strengthening our reputation, advancing our position in the strategic intelligence category, and supporting the company’s continued growth.

Reporting to the Head of Global Marketing & Communications, the Director will serve as a trusted communications partner to the CEO and senior leadership team. You will translate Strider’s strategy, technology, intelligence capabilities, and perspective on the evolving geopolitical landscape into compelling narratives that support business and commercial priorities.

You will lead communications across our primary markets in the United States, United Kingdom, and EMEA, while supporting growing opportunities in Japan and Australia. This is an opportunity to shape the next stage of Strider’s communications function, develop a growing team, and build the frameworks that enable strong, consistent execution across global markets.




KEY QUALIFICATIONS


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years of experience in corporate communications, public relations, executive communications, or a related field, including experience leading communications programs for a growing organization.

 - Experience developing corporate narratives and translating complex business, technology, security, intelligence, or industry topics into clear and compelling communications for varied audiences.

 - Exceptional writing and editorial skills across executive communications, media materials, presentations, thought leadership, and long-form content.

 - Demonstrated media relations experience, including proactive media engagement, spokesperson preparation, and communications for sensitive or high-profile issues.

 - Experience advising executives and senior leaders on communications strategy, messaging, thought leadership, and external positioning.

 - Experience building communications processes, frameworks, and measurement practices that enable effective execution across teams and markets.

 - Experience connecting communications strategy and priorities to broader business and commercial objectives.

 - Experience leading and developing communications teams and managing agencies or other external partners.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience in national security, geopolitical risk, strategic intelligence, cybersecurity, defense, technology, or another complex or highly regulated industry.

 - Experience leading communications across multiple global markets, particularly the United States, United Kingdom, and EMEA.

 - Experience building or scaling a corporate communications function.

 - Experience developing or overseeing analyst relations programs.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.




DESCRIPTION


CORPORATE COMMUNICATIONS & REPUTATION

 - Develop and execute Strider’s global corporate communications strategy in alignment with company priorities, commercial objectives, and brand positioning.

 - Own and evolve Strider’s corporate narrative, messaging architecture, and key messages across audiences and markets.

 - Lead communications for major company moments, including announcements, partnerships, milestones, organizational changes, and market expansion.

 - Partner across Marketing, Sales, Intelligence, Product, People Operations, and other teams to maintain a clear and cohesive Strider story.

 - Anticipate emerging issues and reputational considerations and lead communications planning for sensitive or crisis situations.

 - Establish processes, measurement practices, and operating rhythms that strengthen the communications function as Strider grows.




EXECUTIVE COMMUNICATIONS, THOUGHT LEADERSHIP & CONTENT

 - Serve as a strategic communications advisor to the CEO and senior leadership team.

 - Develop executive messaging, presentations, speeches, bylined articles, social content, and preparation materials for media and speaking engagements.

 - Build thought leadership programs that strengthen Strider’s position on strategic intelligence, technology, security, geopolitical risk, and related issues.

 - Partner with Strider’s Intelligence team to turn original research and differentiated expertise into signature reports and compelling thought leadership.

 - Lead the editorial strategy and content direction for the Strider blog.

 - Support Strider-hosted events through agenda development, executive messaging, and speaker preparation.




MEDIA & ANALYST RELATIONS

 - Lead Strider’s media strategy and build relationships with relevant journalists and industry influencers in partnership with our external PR agency.

 - Serve as a company spokesperson and oversee media inquiries, press releases, statements, briefing materials, and other external communications.

 - Develop proactive media strategies that increase awareness and understanding of Strider’s capabilities, leadership, market perspective, and business momentum.

 - Develop Strider’s analyst relations strategy and oversee the program as it grows, building relationships with relevant analysts and research firms.




GLOBAL COMMUNICATIONS & TEAM LEADERSHIP

 - Lead and develop Strider’s communications team, expanding the team’s capabilities and ownership as the function grows.

 - Create communications frameworks, guidance, and tools that enable regional teams to execute effectively while maintaining a consistent global narrative.

 - Manage Strider’s external PR agency and other communications partners, establishing clear priorities, expectations, and measures of success.

 - Partner with regional teams to adapt communications for audiences in the United States, United Kingdom, and EMEA while supporting growth in Japan and Australia.

 - Partner with People Operations on internal communications, with a focus on executive messaging, company strategy, major announcements, and organizational change.




WHY JOIN STRIDER?

 - Shape Strider’s global story. Help define the corporate voice and reputation of a growing company working at the intersection of AI, intelligence, security, and geopolitical risk.

 - Partner with senior leadership. Advise Strider’s leaders on communications surrounding some of the company’s most important priorities and moments.

 - Build for the next stage of growth. Develop a communications team, operating model, and global capabilities designed to scale with the business.

 - Turn expertise into influence. Work alongside Strider’s Intelligence team to transform differentiated expertise and original research into compelling thought leadership.

 - Make an impact across markets. Help tell Strider’s story in established global markets while building the communications foundation for continued international growth.

Strider is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and do not discriminate against employees or applicants based on race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We comply with all relevant employment laws in the locations where we operate. This commitment applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, promotion, compensation, and professional development.

Provide services and support as an Engineering Functional Area Senior Electrical Field Engineer – Construction (CO102) under Labor Category: Construction Discipline Engineer at Savannah River Site / Aiken, South Carolina.  Senior Electrical Field Engineer – Construction - Engineering (CO102) works collaboratively as part of the ProSidian Engagement Team as Exempt personnel.  Dedicated Planned Labor Hours (DPLH) of 2080 Straight Time (ST) Estimated Annual Quantity (Hrs. Per Yr.) | 300 Overtime Time (OT) Estimated Annual Quantity (Hrs. Per Yr.).  This is a Labor Hour Subcontract or Contract W-2 (IRS-1099) position, and ProSidian reserves the right to convert to a full-time ProSidian-employed W-2 Position.

The role(s) are located at Savannah River Site / Aiken, South Carolina, with an identified Work Site Address (121 Richland Ave E, Aiken, SC 29801, USA), providing Engineering functions working to provide BOA Support Services for multiple department requirement Service Areas (SA) for Savannah River Remediation LLC (The SRMC/LW Contractor) at the U.S. Department of Energy | Savannah River Site (DOE-SRS) in Aiken, SC to support the evolving needs of the organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Senior Electrical Field Engineer – Construction - Engineering (CO102)

Role Scope: Plan and provide technical oversight of field construction procurement, fabrication, installation, modification, and maintenance of systems and components within the assigned discipline.

• Design coordination: Coordinate with design agencies for timely issuance of new designs and design changes. Resolve construction design problems with Design Engineers.
• Constructability reviews: Review design output and vendor documents. Conduct field walkdowns with design engineers. Verify constructability, procedure and code compliance, field conditions against design output, and material availability. Submit constructability comments, track comments to resolution, and support project design review meetings.
• Material takeoff and procurement: Develop and expedite bills of materials (BOM). Track material delivery progress and status. Coordinate delivery to the field. Verify received materials against ordered materials.
• Work execution plan development: Conduct walkdowns with craft supervision and support groups. Develop installation sequences and work instructions. Generate inspection and test records or coordinate with Quality Control. Identify layout and survey needs and generate requests. Prepare job-specific hazard analyses and support or lead team hazard-analysis review meetings.
• Permits and authorizations: Generate or support job-specific permits and orders as required: lockout/tagout orders, power services utilization permits, hot work, asbestos disturbance, confined space, radiological work, excavation, and hazardous waste.
• Work plan review and approval: Attend or chair execution-plan review meetings. Develop hazard-analysis and work-plan approval routing lists. Coordinate and expedite work-package approval routing. Disposition review comments. Assemble approved work execution plans. Provide plan status and updates in the SRS work control passport system.
• Field execution support: Lead craft pre-job briefings. Perform task-ready walkdowns with craft supervision. Verify installed commodity quantities. Coordinate daily field support. Expedite or order materials as required. Coordinate material testing and track shop fabrication supporting field execution. Perform field inspections and identify and coordinate resolution of installation issues.
• Quality compliance: Inspect and verify materials, equipment, and workmanship against drawings, specifications, and applicable codes. Coordinate with Quality Control to confirm installation requirements are met.
• Turnover and startup: Participate in turnover activities and support startup and functional checkout of equipment and systems.
• Work plan closure: Generate design completion notices. Ensure work execution plan status accuracy. Close required permits and work execution plan documentation.

Desired Qualifications For Senior Electrical Field Engineer – Construction - Engineering (CO102) Candidates:

• Required: Thorough understanding of construction engineering and construction electrical engineering principles and ability to apply them to field conditions.
• Required: Working knowledge of discipline-specific codes and standards.
• Required: Previous experience generating computer-based construction work execution plans or work packages, including job-specific hazard analysis. Asset Suite and Assisted Hazard Analysis or equivalent are identified in the description. Asset Suite experience is preferred.
• Required: Previous experience generating job hazard analyses.
• Required: Previous experience performing material takeoffs and procurement.
• Required: Capability to obtain qualification to work in radiological work areas.

CONSTRUCTION DISCIPLINE ENGINEER ELECTRICAL

The position requires the following specific requirements:

• Thorough understanding of Construction Electrical Engineering principles and the ability to apply these principles to field conditions
• Familiar with the National Electrical Code (NEC). The candidate shall be familiar with power distribution, controls, and instrumentation, and be able to read schematics (motors, pumps, distribution centers, etc.).
• Knowledge of SRS-specific electrical guides and standards is a plus
• Experience in radiological work planning and hazard analysis is desirable
• Capable of climbing and spending extended periods of time in the field
• Capable of obtaining qualification to work in radiological work areas

Education / Experience Requirements / Qualifications

• Alternative 1: Bachelor’s degree in the specified engineering discipline AND at least 5 years of practical construction field engineering experience in that discipline.
• Alternative 2: Associate’s degree in the specified engineering discipline AND 5–10 years of practical construction engineering experience in that discipline.
• Alternative 3: High school diploma AND 10+ years of practical construction engineering experience in the specified discipline.

Discipline applicability: Meet one of the three alternative education/experience pathways. Specified discipline is Mechanical, Piping, Electrical, Civil, or Instruments and Controls, as determined by the requestor. This supplied specialization is Electrical.

• Required: Thorough understanding of construction engineering and construction electrical engineering principles and ability to apply them to field conditions.

• Required: Previous experience generating job hazard analyses.

Skills Required

Primarily focused on Senior Electrical Field Engineer – Construction initiatives and aligned with Program Support activities in the Engineering Functional Area.
