You might be drawn to our innovative approach and refusal to settle for the “way things have always been done.” Or you could find it exciting to grow your skills while working for an industry-leading brand. Whether you’re into our values, our brand, or our egg-cellent puns, we hope you’ll join our Crew and help us change the world 108 square feet at a time!

At Vital Farms, we’re proud of the diverse communities we serve and the stakeholders who help bring our purpose to life. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative environment where every crew member feels valued. We see this as one of our greatest strengths - and your role is key to helping us build on it.

Your Role:

At Vital Farms, we believe in cultivating a people-first experience grounded in integrity, transparency, and operational excellence. The People Generalist plays a key role in delivering exceptional HR support to our crew and the People Team. This role is responsible for executing core HR processes and providing timely, accurate support related to attendance, payroll assistance, onboarding, systems upkeep, and employment documentation.  As the first point of contact for People-related system inquiries, this role ensures smooth operations and a positive crew experience by managing the Vital HR email inbox and supporting a wide range of administrative and systems-based HR functions.

What You'll Do:

• - Maintain a consistent, highly visible presence on the plant floor across shifts. Spend the majority of working time close to crew members and operations, proactively building relationships, observing needs firsthand, and addressing questions and opportunities at the source.

• - Provide employee relations support by responding to routine concerns, coaching supervisors on policy application and next steps, supporting corrective action documentation, assisting with investigations, and coordinating termination and offboarding processes when needed.

• - Provide significant onsite learning and development support by assessing local needs and designing, coordinating, and facilitating practical training, orientation content, policy rollouts, and crew education across shifts.

• - Serve as an accessible leadership coach for supervisors and managers, providing real-time coaching, reinforcing effective people leadership practices, and helping leaders translate learning into consistent actions on the plant floor.

• - Use regular plant-floor engagement to identify emerging crew, leadership, learning, and operational needs; turn those observations into timely coaching, practical solutions, and innovative improvements.

• - Manage HRIS administration in UKG, including new hire setup, employee record maintenance, E-Verify completion, status changes, transfers, department moves, reporting structure updates, timeclock assignments, onboarding activities, and basic system troubleshooting.

• - Run routine and ad hoc reports, including attendance, headcount, turnover, staffing, labor, workforce maintenance, and other reports requested by leaders or the People Team.

• - Review attendance reports and point balances, audit attendance accuracy, support attendance point administration, and guide supervisors through attendance discipline levels and policy application.

• - Assist with payroll preparation, payroll audits, timekeeping review, missed punches, punch exceptions, and timekeeping discrepancies, including support during regular payroll cycles and holiday weeks.

• - Manage unemployment claims and documentation by gathering supporting records, coordinating responses, and partnering with leadership and the People Team on hearings and claim follow-up.

• - Complete employee verification requests accurately and confidentially, and maintain personnel files, HR documentation, and records in alignment with retention and compliance expectations.

• - Partner closely with Talent Acquisition partners and site leaders to support workforce planning, recruiting, and staffing needs.

• - Assist with escalated Talent Acquisition and crew member concerns that require People Team support, including rehire eligibility reviews, and availability verification.

• - Support crew engagement activities, recognition programs, communication, event execution, and other employee experience initiatives as needed.

• - Think innovatively about crew engagement, leader development, and People processes; identify practical improvements, test new approaches, and contribute to SOP creation, documentation, team meetings, and local People Team support.

What You Bring to the Table:

• - At least 3–5 years of experience in human resources, employee relations, People operations, payroll, or a related People function.

• - Experience supporting a manufacturing or other high-volume worksite preferred.

• - Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, or a related field preferred, or equivalent work experience.

• - Working knowledge of employee relations practices, People policies, corrective action, investigations, and documentation expectations.

• - Experience supporting HRIS, payroll, timekeeping, reporting, onboarding, E-Verify, unemployment, and personnel recordkeeping processes; UKG experience preferred.

• - Demonstrated experience facilitating onsite learning, coaching frontline leaders, and delivering crew-facing training and communication in a practical, engaging, and approachable way.

• - Strong desire and demonstrated ability to work primarily onsite and on the plant floor, with the flexibility to build relationships and support crew members and leaders across shifts.

• - Ability to flex work hours to support business needs, including nights, weekends, and holidays as needed.

• - Strong customer-service mindset with the ability to support crew members and leaders with professionalism, confidentiality, and follow-through.

• - Excellent attention to detail, organization, prioritization, and ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

• - Strong communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships across shifts, departments, supervisors, managers, and People Team partners.

• - Proactive, dependable, and comfortable working independently while knowing when to escalate sensitive or complex situations.

• - Strong computer skills and ability to use applications such as Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and HR systems.

• - Ability to travel 10–20% of the time for company meetings, team offsites, or training sessions.

• - You’re no hero – You know the power of teamwork and celebrate the work of others before your own.

• - You give a sh*t – You believe in acting like an owner and making Vital Farms a place to be proud of.

jobs.title: Sr. Recruiter, High Volume Manufacturing (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. RECRUITER, HIGH VOLUME MANUFACTURING (STARLINK)

We are looking for highly motivated, full-life cycle recruiters to support Starlink manufacturing, driving the high volume recruiting that unlocks one of the most complex manufacturing operations on earth. We are seeking a creative thinker who can leverage both traditional and non-traditional approaches to identifying excellent talent and has a deep-seated passion for Starlink’s mission to connect the unconnected.

Successful candidates will have outstanding communication skills, be self-motivated, hold themselves accountable, have a willingness and drive to manage a demanding high-volume workload, strong presentation skills, and experience working successfully in a team environment. Comfortable communicating with all levels of stakeholders.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

As a SpaceX recruiter, you will run a full desk with a variety of duties and responsibilities focused on the sourcing, screening, interviewing, and onboarding of top talent candidates to fill mission critical positions. In many cases, you are candidates’ first encounter with SpaceX, and it is your job to represent the company with professionalism, pride, and enthusiasm. We work in teams and focus on collaboration yet require a high degree of autonomy. So, while you are not expected to simply go at it alone, you are expected to show initiative, take responsibility, and run with tasks to completion.

Your day-to-day routine will change often as hiring priorities shift, but there is a basic set of activities you can expect to run daily, including, but not limited to:

• Review internal and external applications, conduct passive candidate searches, interview candidates, and act as a consultative recruiting partner to clients

• Deeply understand each role's requirements and how it fits into the organization

• Develop and execute strategies focused on creating and maintaining a strong pipeline of passive talent

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients and candidates through clear and consistent communication

• Find creative ways to capture the attention of candidates during initial outreach stages

• Manage a high volume of clients and requisitions

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of recruiting experience; or associate degree and 6+ years of experience; or 7+ years of professional experience as a recruiter in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 2+ years of high-volume recruiting experience, ideally in the manufacturing sector

• Experience with in-house recruiting

• Experience recruiting for skilled trades (technicians, electricians, facilities, etc.)

• Strong tenure with demonstrated success in recruiting roles

• Full life cycle recruiting experience, from sourcing to closing

• Comfort with reviewing, evaluating and reporting on recruiting data

• Ability to distinguish between the top 50% and the top 5% of talent within their respective fields

• Demonstrated expertise in non-standard recruiting methods: cold calling candidates and companies, organizing and executing ad hoc networking events, identifying industry experts and finding unique methods to engage with them, creating unique targeted sourcing campaigns, etc.

• Comfortable interfacing directly with hiring managers including director and VP level technical leaders

• Ability to build strong relationships with both hiring managers and candidates

• Ability to accurately present but not oversell candidates to client groups; influence decisions by acting as the subject matter expert on talent but avoid dictating client decisions

• Ability to multi-task and operate with little direction while still being an active team member

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed

• This position is based in Bastrop, TX (Austin area), and requires being onsite full-time – hybrid and remote work will not be considered

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Linux Kernel Engineer - Avionics SW
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

We're looking for an experienced Linux kernel engineer to own and solve hard problems across hardware, firmware, kernel, and userspace on our embedded flight computers. You will set the technical direction for the kernel and platform work, as well as bring up new hardware, develop and maintain kernel drivers, and debug system-level issues, and shape how we build and validate kernel software as the platform scales to millions of deliveries every single day.

As a Senior or Staff Linux kernel engineer at Zipline, you will be responsible for stability and performance of the Linux kernel, which is the foundation of our flight computers. The kernel operates as a safety-critical software layer that will enable our aircraft to safely make millions of deliveries a day. You'll own the kernel drivers, hardware bring-up, and system-level debugging that the rest of the flight software stack depends on.

You will work closely with hardware, firmware, platform, networking, and flight software teams, from the first boot of a new board to diagnosing rare failures across a deployed fleet. You'll help define what "ready to ship" means and build the validation that backs it up.

You will also help build reusable kernel tooling, diagnostics, and automated tests that level up our systems' observability and reliability. At the Staff level, you will set the technical direction for kernel and platform work, not just execute it.

What You'll Do

• Diagnose crashes, hangs, races, driver failures, and performance or timing problems across a deployed fleet using crash dumps, kernel traces, logs, and telemetry, and turn rare field failures into reproducible tests.

• Drive ambiguous, cross-system issues from investigation to validated resolution, then invest in tooling, testing, and architecture so they don't come back.

• Develop, debug, and maintain Linux kernel drivers and related subsystems, and own them end to end.

• Design for failure: define how the kernel and drivers detect, contain, and recover from faults (watchdogs, error handling paths, graceful degradation), and verify that behavior on real hardware.

• Bring up new hardware, including device tree configuration, firmware interfaces, and board-support software.

• Build diagnostics, benchmarks, and automated tests that catch regressions before they ship.

• Measure and improve latency, throughput, CPU and memory use, and networking performance.

• Serve as a technical reviewer for kernel and driver changes, and maintain our patch stack across kernel upgrades.

• Write and review design docs, and drive cross-team technical decisions to consensus with hardware, firmware, platform, networking, and flight software teams.

• Mentor engineers and raise the team's bar for code quality, debugging practice, and testing.

• Contribute patches upstream and track upstream regressions that affect us.

What You'll Bring

• 7+ years of professional Linux kernel work, including ownership of at least one driver, subsystem, or hardware bring-up from start to finish.

• Strong C and deep familiarity with kernel internals: scheduling, interrupts, concurrency, memory management, DMA, MMIO, and the Linux device model.

• A record of debugging on real hardware and reading datasheets or interface specs to find root causes.

• Fluency with kernel debugging and measurement tools such as ftrace, perf, dynamic debug, and crash analysis, and the habit of validating fixes with data.

• Comfort with the upstream patch workflow.

• Experience writing design docs, leading technical efforts across teams, and mentoring other engineers.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining a subtle kernel problem to people who don't work in the kernel.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience in one or more of these areas is a plus:
